Northeastern Design System · Organism · GlobalHeaderv0.1 · 2026-11-17

GlobalHeader

The university bar every official site carries, unaltered: the lockup, the six sections, search, More, and Give. Night by default; transparent with a top shade over a film, solid over content, compact (monogram only) once the page scrolls. Below 960px the sections fold into the MobileMenu.

Found on

Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
variantsolid | over-mediasolidOver-media only on a page that opens with a HeroFrame or a full-bleed photograph; it turns solid once the hero scrolls away.
compactbooleanfalseThe scrolled state: 64px bar, monogram only. The page sets it after the first 72px of scroll.
modedark | lightdarkNight everywhere by default. Light is a template choice for sites that open on Canvas, never a per-site restyle.
logobooleantrueFalse only when the LocalHeader carries the lockup (brand: one logo per page). The bar keeps its centred sections.
sectionsNavTrigger[]the sixAdmissions, Experiential learning, Research, Global, Entrepreneurship, AI. Fixed by the university, not by sites.
currentsection keynoneSets aria-current on that NavTrigger when the page lives in a university section.
giveButtonGiveOutline, small. It turns red on hover (22a). The one Accent of the page belongs to the page, not the bar.
<header class="nu-global-header" data-mode="dark">
  <div class="nu-global-header__bar">
    <a class="nu-global-header__brand" href="https://www.northeastern.edu/"><svg class="nu-logo" role="img" aria-label="Northeastern University">…</svg></a>
    <nav class="nu-global-header__nav" aria-label="Northeastern University"><ul>
      <li><button class="nu-nav-trigger" type="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="mm-admissions">Admissions <svg class="nu-icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-chevron-down"></use></svg></button></li>
      …
      <li><a class="nu-nav-trigger" href="/ai/">AI</a></li>
    </ul></nav>
    <div class="nu-global-header__actions">
      <button class="nu-icon-button" type="button" aria-label="Search Northeastern" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="search">…</button>
      <button class="nu-nav-trigger nu-global-header__more" type="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="mm-more">More …</button>
      <button class="nu-icon-button nu-global-header__menu" type="button" aria-label="Open menu" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="menu">…</button>
      <a class="nu-button nu-button--sm nu-button--outline" href="https://giving.northeastern.edu/">Give</a>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="nu-mega-menu" id="mm-admissions" hidden>…</div>
</header>

Events

  • open-section { id } when a NavTrigger opens its MegaMenu; any other open panel closes.
  • open-search Opens the SearchOverlay and moves focus to its field.
  • open-menu Opens the MobileMenu (below 960px).

Accessibility

  • A <header> with one <nav aria-label="Northeastern University">, so it is distinct from the LocalHeader's nav.
  • Triggers are buttons with aria-expanded and aria-controls; Escape closes the panel and returns focus.
  • The lockup link is named Northeastern University by the Logo's role="img".
  • A skip link to the main content comes before the header (template).
  • Over film, the shade guarantees 4.5:1 for the labels on the brightest frame; check each new film.

Usage

  • Let the page decide over-media versus solid; the header has no opinion about the hero.
  • Collapse to the monogram on scroll, never hide the bar entirely on desktop.
  • Add, rename or reorder sections for one site: site navigation is the LocalHeader.
  • Show the lockup here and in the LocalHeader.
  • Red on Night: the Give hover is the only red the bar shows.

        …
      </ul>
    </div>

Events

  • close Escape, a click outside, or opening another section. Focus returns to the trigger.

Accessibility

  • A plain region after its trigger in source order: no role="menu", so the links keep normal Tab behaviour.
  • Column headings are real headings (h3) under the panel title (h2).
  • Every link row is 44px tall.
  • The story is one link (StoryCard), named by its headline.

Usage

  • Keep the lead sentence to one line of plain description.
  • Order columns from task to browse: Apply before Academics.
  • More than three link columns or a second story.
  • Icons beside links, or bold link text.
  • Open on hover alone.

SearchOverlay

Site-wide search, opened from the GlobalHeader's search button: a Night band over the top of the page with the underline SearchField at full measure, a close button, and five popular destinations as outline pills. A full Scrim dims the page beneath. Submit goes to the results page; nothing searches as you type.

Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
actionurlhttps://search.northeastern.eduA GET form with query, so results have a shareable URL and work without script.
scopetextSearch NortheasternThe label and placeholder. A LocalHeader search names its site instead: Search the Global Experience Office.
popularLink[]fiveDestinations, not query suggestions. Chosen by the web team from search logs; three to six.
openbooleanfalsehidden when closed. Opening moves focus into the field.
<div class="nu-search-overlay" id="search" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Search Northeastern" data-mode="dark" hidden>
  <div class="nu-search-overlay__inner">
    <div class="nu-search-overlay__row">
      <form class="nu-search-field nu-search-field--underline" role="search" action="https://search.northeastern.edu">…</form>
      <button class="nu-icon-button" type="button" aria-label="Close search">…</button>
    </div>
    <nav class="nu-search-overlay__popular" aria-labelledby="search-pop">
      <h2 class="nu-text nu-text--label" id="search-pop">Popular</h2>
      <ul><li><a class="nu-button nu-button--sm nu-button--outline" href="https://admissions.northeastern.edu/">Undergraduate admissions</a></li> …</ul>
    </nav>
  </div>
</div>

Events

  • submit { query }, native GET.
  • close The close button, Escape, or a click on the scrim. Focus returns to the search button.

Accessibility

  • role="dialog" with aria-modal and the name Search Northeastern; focus is trapped in the band while open.
  • The field has a real (visually hidden) label; submit is a labelled Search button, not an icon.
  • Popular links are a nav named by its visible heading.
  • The page behind is inert while the overlay is open.

Usage

  • Keep the placeholder to the scope: Search Northeastern.
  • Send people to one results page for the whole university.
  • Live results under the field on a site-wide search.
  • Popular pills that duplicate the MegaMenu's overview links one for one.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · MobileMenuv0.1 · 2026-11-17

MobileMenu

The GlobalHeader below 960px: a full-screen Night sheet with the monogram and a close button where the bar was, the underline search, and each section as an AccordionItem set large and light. Open, a section leads with its overview links as outline pills, then its links under small headings. Smaller destinations and Give close the sheet.

          <div class="nu-accordion-item__panel">

Events

  • close The close button or Escape; focus returns to the Menu button.
  • toggle Native details toggle per group.

Accessibility

  • role="dialog", aria-modal, named Menu; the page behind is inert and does not scroll.
  • Groups are native details/summary with the section name as an h2: state and keyboard come free.
  • Every link row is 44px; pills are 44px Buttons.
  • The close button sits exactly where the Menu button was.

Usage

  • Keep the order and names identical to the desktop sections.
  • Put the one overview link of each section first, as a pill.
  • A third level: sections hold links, not more accordions.
  • Slide-in drawers that leave a sliver of the page visible.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · LocalHeaderv0.1 · 2026-11-17

LocalHeader

On unit sites the unit's row now lives in HeaderStack (continuous); LocalHeader is the standalone bar for a site that carries the lockup itself, and its section-menu parts are reused there. A unit site's own bar, under the GlobalHeader: the SiteIdentity at the start, the site's sections, search and one optional action at the end. Sticky at 72px once the global bar scrolls away. It follows its ground (Canvas or Night). A section menu is a small floating list under its trigger; below 960px the sections fold behind a Menu button. When it carries the Northeastern lockup, the GlobalHeader drops its own.

Events

  • toggle { section, expanded } from a NavTrigger; one menu open at a time.
  • open-menu Below 960px, opens the site's own MobileMenu sheet.
  • stick The template pins the bar at the top once the GlobalHeader has scrolled past.

Accessibility

  • A second <nav> named for the site (Global Experience Office), distinct from the GlobalHeader's.
  • Menus are lists of links after their trigger, not role="menu"; Escape closes and returns focus.
  • The site name is the link home; the lockup link goes to northeastern.edu.
  • Sticky bars stay within 72px so zoomed pages keep their content.

Usage

  • Write the unit name in full, as officially titled.
  • Keep section labels to one or two words in sentence case.
  • A unit logo, a second monogram, or the lockup in both headers.
  • Seven dropdowns in a row: fold the rest into More.
  • Red text or a red current marker on Night.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · HeaderStackv0.1 · 2026-11-17

HeaderStack

How the university header and a unit's header share the top of a page, so a unit site never reads as two sites stacked. Explore (D) is the system's treatment: a 48px strip with the monogram and Explore Northeastern, which opens the MobileMenu sheet with every university section, search and Give, over the unit's 72px bar. It follows the live sites' Explore Northeastern drawer. Merged, Strip and Continuous stay on the sheet as the alternatives considered (Continuous was tried on the templates 2026-10-30 and read as two navs still), with today's two full bars for comparison. Every treatment keeps one search, one Give and one lockup.

Organism
Class

Composes
GlobalHeader, MobileMenu, SiteIdentity, NavTrigger, IconButton, Button, Logo
Used by
Campaign / competition, Detail with section nav, Event, Finder page, Not found, Program / location, Search results, Section hub, Unit home
Found on

Events

  • navigate Native link and button behaviour; menus open as in LocalHeader.

Accessibility

  • Two navigation landmarks, labelled by owner: Northeastern University and the unit's name.
  • One search control, labelled for what it searches.
  • Every target is at least 44px; the strip's small type still sits in 44px hit areas.

Usage

  • Use Explore on every unit site; Explore Northeastern opens the MobileMenu sheet at every width; the unit's action button (Contact, Apply) sits at the end of its row and moves into Menu on phones.
  • Keep one search and one Give across the whole stack.
  • Two full-height bars of equal weight.
  • A search in each bar.
  • The lockup in both rows.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · SectionNavv0.1 · 2026-11-17

SectionNav

The pages of one section beside the content, replacing nuin's red sidebars: a back link to the parent, the section's name, then a ruled list. The current page is Medium with a 2px marker in the margin, red on Canvas and canvas on Night; its branch opens one nested level. Below 960px it becomes a disclosure above the content that names the page you are on. The horizontal form (SiblingNav) sets two to seven sibling pages as one row of links on a hairline under a hero: a pathway switcher, Team / Leadership, or a campaign's own pages.

Level
Organism
Class
.nu-section-nav __parent __title __list __link __disclosure __summary __summary-page --horizontal __label
Composes
NavLink, ArrowLink, Heading, Link, Rule, IconButton, Text
Used by
Detail with section nav, SiblingNav
Found on
global (nuin) M10: red sidebar with a « Back to button and sibling links, no current-page state (77 pages); global (nuin) M11–M12: red descriptive card sidebar; plain list sidebar; experiential: overlay menu as the only local navigation; research: no section navigation at all (gap); experiential el-07: Professional / Academic / Extracurricular switcher set as a primary pill, with no current state; external affairs ea-12: Team / Leadership as filter Chips; entrepreneurship ge-08: the four Next Up pages joined only by a breadcrumb

Housing

Where you will live during your semester in Greece, what each residence includes, and how to settle in.

Every N.U.in Greece student lives in program housing arranged with the partner institution. Rooms are furnished, and each residence lists its amenities, meals, laundry and mail below, with photographs of a typical room.

Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
parentArrowLinknoneBack to the level above: The N.U.in Program. Omit at the top of a site.
title{text, href}requiredThe section's name, linking to its overview page. A Heading at h4 size; its level follows the page outline (usually h2).
pages{text, href, children?}[]requiredSiblings in the editor's order. Children show only under the current branch: one nested level, never two.
currenthrefrequiredaria-current="page" on the page, aria-current="true" on its parent when the page is nested.
collapsedbooleanbelow 960pxThe disclosure form: the summary names the section and the current page.
orientationvertical | horizontalverticalHorizontal is the SiblingNav: no parent link or title; an optional __label (meta text: the section or campaign name) leads the row from 720px. Two to seven pages, one to three words each. Below 720px the row scrolls inside itself; the page never scrolls sideways.
<nav class="nu-section-nav" aria-label="N.U.in Greece">
  <a class="nu-arrow-link nu-arrow-link--sm nu-arrow-link--back nu-section-nav__parent" href="/nuin/">…The N.U.in Program</a>
  <h2 class="nu-heading nu-heading--h4 nu-section-nav__title"><a href="/nuin/greece/">N.U.in Greece</a></h2>
  <ul class="nu-section-nav__list">
    <li><a class="nu-section-nav__link nu-nav-link" href="/nuin/greece/important-dates/">Important dates</a></li>
    <li><a class="nu-section-nav__link nu-nav-link" href="/nuin/greece/housing/" aria-current="page">Housing</a></li>
    <li><a class="nu-section-nav__link nu-nav-link" href="/nuin/greece/health-and-safety/" aria-current="true">Health and safety</a>
      <ul class="nu-section-nav__list"><li><a class="nu-section-nav__link nu-nav-link" href="…">Insurance</a></li> …</ul></li>
  </ul>
</nav>

<!-- Horizontal (SiblingNav) -->
<nav class="nu-section-nav nu-section-nav--horizontal" aria-label="Experiential opportunities">
  <ul class="nu-section-nav__list">
    <li><a class="nu-section-nav__link nu-nav-link" href="/experiential-opportunities/professional/">Professional</a></li>
    <li><a class="nu-section-nav__link nu-nav-link" href="/experiential-opportunities/academic/" aria-current="page">Academic</a></li>
    <li><a class="nu-section-nav__link nu-nav-link" href="/experiential-opportunities/extracurricular/">Extracurricular</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>

Events

  • toggle Native details toggle in the collapsed form.

Accessibility

  • A <nav> named for the section (N.U.in Greece), so it is told apart from the site navigation.
  • Current page by aria-current="page", shown by weight and the marker, never colour alone.
  • Every row, nested ones included, is 44px tall; horizontal links are 48px tall.
  • Horizontal: the same <nav> + <ul> + aria-current="page"; the label is a <p>, and the nav keeps its own aria-label so the label is not the only name.
  • The disclosure is native details/summary.

Usage

  • Keep labels to the page titles, shortened only when the title repeats the section (Greece housing → Housing).
  • Put the nav first in source on phones (above the content), after the content heading on desktop.
  • Horizontal: put it directly under the hero, the same row on every sibling page, in the same order, so the switcher never moves.
  • Red fields, white-on-red text or icons as bullets (nuin's sidebar).
  • More than one nested level: split the section instead.
  • A red marker on Night.
  • Horizontal: Chips or pill Buttons for sibling pages (they read as filters or calls to action); anchors to sections of one page (that is ChapterRail or ContentsBar); the bare row as a page section: SiblingNav (organisms/sibling-nav) wraps it as a flush, bleed bar with a travelling form and a gliding marker.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · AlertBarv0.1 · 2026-11-17

AlertBar

The one site-wide notice: a full-width band above the GlobalHeader that scrolls away with it. It is Notice's site variant placed on the page, its content aligned to the header's edge. Info and warning are dismissible and remembered; an emergency is not, and sits on the raised ground.

Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
toneinfo | warning | errorinfoError only for emergencies (campus closure, safety); it implies emergency.

<aside class="nu-alert-bar" aria-label="Site alert">
  <div class="nu-notice nu-notice--site nu-notice--info">
    <svg class="nu-icon nu-notice__icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-info"></use></svg>
    <div class="nu-notice__body">
      <p class="nu-text nu-text--small">Interested in studying abroad at Northeastern University London?</p>
      <a class="nu-arrow-link nu-arrow-link--sm" href="https://www.nulondon.ac.uk/">Learn more and apply <svg class="nu-icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-arrow"></use></svg></a>
    </div>
    <button class="nu-icon-button nu-notice__dismiss" type="button" aria-label="Dismiss alert">…</button>
  </div>
</aside>

Events

  • dismiss { id }; the bar is removed and the id stored.

Accessibility

  • An <aside aria-label="Site alert"> before the header in source, after the skip link.
  • Present on load: no live region. An emergency pushed mid-visit uses role="alert".
  • The dismiss control is named Dismiss alert.
  • Tone is carried by the icon and the words, never the fill; the error icon is a graphic (3:1), never red text.

Usage

  • Keep one alert per site at a time, and take it down when it is out of date.
  • Say what to do in the link: Learn more and apply, Read the rules.
  • A red or yellow band (GEO's): the fill is the sunken ground; tone is the icon.
  • Marketing that runs for months: that is a Closer or a MediaText on the page.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · LocalFooterv0.1 · 2026-11-17

LocalFooter

The unit's own footer, directly above the GlobalFooter: its name and how to reach it (address, phone, email, its social accounts) on the left, its link columns on the right, and an optional closing line with one action. It follows its ground and opens on a strong rule, so the black GlobalFooter reads as the separate, university-wide layer.

Northeastern Design System · Organism · GlobalFooterv0.1 · 2026-11-17

GlobalFooter

The footer every official site ends on, required and unaltered (brand): the lockup with the Boston address and switchboard, the university's social accounts, seven link columns, the fourteen campuses, the legal row with cookie preferences, and the Northeastern University wordmark set the full width of the page as its last line. Always Night, on the sunken black ground.

Events

  • cookie-preferences The Cookie preferences button opens the consent manager (TrustArc).

Accessibility

  • The page's one <footer> landmark at the top level (contentinfo).
  • Two navs, named: Northeastern University, more and Campuses.
  • Every social link names the account (Northeastern on Instagram).
  • Cookie preferences is a <button> styled as a link: it opens a dialog, it does not navigate.
  • Rows are 36px with a pointer and 44px below 720px.
  • The giant wordmark is decorative (aria-hidden); the lockup carries the name.

Usage

  • End every page on it, after the LocalFooter.
  • Keep link labels in sentence case.
  • Recolour it to a unit palette or put it on Canvas.
  • Add a unit's links here: they belong in the LocalFooter.
  • Crop or restyle the wordmark.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · HeroPagev0.1 · 2026-11-17

HeroPage

The photo hero of a section page: the page’s H1 on the content edge over the scene scrim, a lead, and optionally a Breadcrumb above and one action below. Tall for section hubs, medium for their children; split sets the words on the page’s own ground with the photograph meeting the right edge.

Level
Organism
Class
.nu-hero-page __media __copy __mark __facts __figure __qualifier --medium --split --display --stack
Composes
Image, Scrim, Breadcrumb, Heading, Text, Button, MetaList, Tag, Stat, KeyValue
Used by
Section hub, Unit home
Found on
22a .hx shade, without the film; nuin M5–M7: full-height, section-parent and ~400 short banner heroes; research: gradient image banners with a text box; global: uppercase H1s and H3 ledes (fixed: sentence case, a lead paragraph); entrepreneurship E1: full-bleed photo with an eyebrow (fixed: no eyebrow); review el-05: the home page wore a sub-page hero (fixed: --display); review el-10 / ea-05: phone heroes cropped to black, lettering fighting the H1 (fixed: per-breakpoint focal point, --stack); review ge-01: a campaign's own mark and prize (fixed: __mark, __facts)

Events

  • click The action’s navigation.

Accessibility

  • The scene variants are a Night band; the split variant takes the ground of its page.
  • Check AA on the real pixels under the lead, not the scrim’s end colour; set the focal point so no face sits under the words.
  • No motion: a page hero is still. Motion belongs to HeroFrame, which carries a pause control.

Usage

  • Use medium for the children of a section so the hub stays the tallest page.
  • Keep the H1 short enough to sit on two lines at most.
  • Check every hero at 390px: if the subject is gone, set the phone focus or switch to --stack.
  • Give the home page the display hero and the unit’s name or its one line as the H1; the mission sentence is the lead.
  • An eyebrow naming the parent above the H1: that is the Breadcrumb’s job.
  • A photo whose own lettering sits under the H1 (two sets of big letters): move the focus or change the photo.
  • --display on any page but the unit’s home.
  • A red tile strip overlapping the hero (nuin M8); local navigation is SectionNav.
  • Text on the photograph without the scrim.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · SectionHeaderv0.1 · 2026-11-17

SectionHeader

The heading that opens a section, with its lead and one onward ArrowLink. A family: stacked on the content edge, split across the grid (6 / 6, the default), offset (5, a column of air, 6), a wide heading over a pair of paragraphs (occasional), centred, on the right columns, and at display size for the section that opens a chapter. Heading alignment is a choice per section. Never an eyebrow above it.

Level
Organism
Class
.nu-section-header __body --split --offset --pair __pair --split-5 --split-6 --align-center --align-end --center --display --end __actions
Composes
Heading, Text, ArrowLink
Used by
AwardScale, CallList, CampusAtlas, CampusGlobe, ElStudentStage, FigureLead, Filmstrip, GlobeChapters, GlobeOrbit, GlobeTour, IndexRows, LogoRow, MapWall, MediaStage, MixedRail, NameWall, OffsetPair, PortraitSet, PosterRail, Section, Section hub, StageTabs, StickyScenes, StoryLead, StoryRail, StorySpotlight, UnevenGrid, Unit home
Found on
22a .sechead (display h2 and lede over the research cards); 22a .rows-head; experiential #117: eyebrow ‘learning in action’ over the h2 (fixed: no eyebrow); every site: centred h2 + paragraph + button blocks; design-system audit 2026-11-12: 36 of 43 headings left, 17 of 22 headers the same 4 / 8 split; docs/dx/split (11-13): six layouts of one pair; Zach chose B (6 / 6) as the default, D (offset) as the second, F (wide heading over two paragraphs) once in a while; 4 / 8 retired

What is co-op?

Co-op is our most immersive experiential program—a full-time, months-long professional work experience that positions you not just for a job, but for your future.

As the pioneer and architect of experiential learning since launching our co‑op program in 1909, Northeastern has spent more than a century cultivating embedded, career-aligned opportunities that give students not just work experience but a competitive edge shaped by continuous innovation.

Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
headingtextrequiredAn h2, at most 75 characters and three lines at 1440px. nu-heading--h2; --display sets it at the display-s step.
leadtextnoneOne or two sentences on --measure-lead (45ch, about 60 characters a line).
linkArrowLinknoneOne onward link to the full index of what the section shows: More research on NGN.
linksArrowLink[2–3]none__actions: two or three onward links on one line, a --space-6 gap between them; they wrap on phones. kit.section_header(links=[…]), or kit.header_links([…]) as extra= of _dx.header. Four or more links are a list, not a header's actions.
bodymarkupnone__body takes its column's whole width; a list, a disclosure (AccordionItem) or a nav inside it does too. Stacked, text keeps its measure; in a split, offset or pair the text fills its column.
alignstart | center | endstart--center puts heading, lead and link on the centre axis. --end starts the header on column 7 from 960px.
splitsplit | offset | pairnone--split (the default split): heading on 1–6, body on 7–12, cap tops on one line, the text filling its column. --offset: heading on 1–5, a column of air, body on 7–12. --pair (once in a while, for two real paragraphs): heading across eight columns, then __body > __pair sets the lead on 1–6 and the detail on 7–12, both starting on one line; a link follows the pair under the lead. All stack below 960px. --split-5 and --split-6 are older names for the same 6 / 6. With --end the heading takes the right columns. kit.section_header(split=True | "offset" | "pair").
valignstart | center | endstartSplit and offset only. --align-center, --align-end: the body against the heading's middle or last baseline.
sizeh2 | displayh2--display: the chapter opener, display-s in the display weight, at most 16ch.

  • The heading level follows the outline (h2 in a page, h3 inside a section); the size is a modifier.
  • The link names its destination; never ‘Learn more’.
  • Centring and the right-column offset are visual only: source order stays heading, lead, link.

Usage

  • Choose the alignment per section: centre a heading that stands alone over a wide stage, split one that introduces a row, offset one that sits beside a picture.
  • Split by default; offset where the heading should read as a title beside its own column; pair only for a lead and a real second paragraph, a few times in the whole estate. Column 7 is the reading edge: rows and lists under a split start there.
  • Use split only when the heading fits two lines in its columns; let a long heading run stacked or centred.
  • Use --display once or twice a page, where a chapter opens.
  • Leave the gap below to the system: whatever follows sits one --head-gap under the header.
  • An eyebrow or kicker above the heading.
  • The same header variant three sections running.
  • Colour the heading red, or set a rule on the header: the seam hairline belongs to the section (nu-section--ruled).
Northeastern Design System · Organism · MediaTextv0.1 · 2026-11-17

MediaText

A photograph or film beside its copy on the 12-column grid, with a choice of split (media on 7, 8, 6 or 5 columns, either side), ratio (3:2, 4:5, 1:1, 16:9) and where the copy sits against the picture (top, centre, bottom), so a page's picture-and-copy sections vary on purpose. A run of them at one shape is FeatureRows. The bleed variant runs the picture past the content edge to meet the viewport, as 22a’s spotlight rows do. Works on Canvas and Night.

Events

  • click The actions’ navigation.

Accessibility

  • The media comes first in the DOM only when it is the subject; otherwise the copy does and the grid places the picture.

Usage

  • Alternate sides down a page and keep the copy short enough to sit beside the picture at 1200px.
  • Change the split or the ratio when two MediaTexts share a page: no two consecutive sections share a layout.
  • Use the bleed variant once or twice a page: it is a gesture.
  • On Persuade pages, make the page’s one Night feature an overlay; keep the split rows for Read pages.
  • Three pill buttons in one row (research #318).
  • An overlay on Canvas, or two overlays in a row: it is the page’s feature band.
  • A rounded or shadowed frame, or a coloured panel behind the copy.

Northeastern Design System · Organism · CardGridv0.1 · 2026-11-17

CardGrid

A section of same-kind cards under one heading: stories, people, events or programs. An ArrowLink to the full list sits opposite the heading; a Load more Button follows the grid. Columns follow the section's own width; Skeleton cards hold the slots while loading, and an EmptyState stands in when there is nothing to show. Grouped sets one grid per group (staff by office) with the group heading in columns 1–6; pair sets exactly two stories as a 2-up feature. Bento sets three stories as one lead and two beside it. Stagger drops every other card a step (equals as a rhythm); feature runs the lead full width as a horizontal story with the rest in a row below; list sets a few text-led ruled rows with small photographs.

Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
titletextrequiredHeading h2 (Light, h2 scale), sentence case, under 75 characters. The section, not a kicker: Research news, not LATEST.
introtextnoneOne sentence under the heading.
linkArrowLinknoneTo the full list: All research stories. Never Learn more.
itemsStoryCard[] | PersonCard[] | EventCard[] | ProgramCard[]requiredOne kind per grid. In a <ul role="list">, one card per item.
columns3 | 43Four for people and small cards; three for stories, events and programs. 1 → 2 → 3/4 at 720 and 960px of the grid's width.
moreButtonnoneLoad more stories. Busy while loading (aria-busy, Spinner); removed when everything shows.
groups{title, intro?, items}[]none--grouped: each group is a <section> with its heading (h3) and count in columns 1–6 and its cards from column 7. Leaders first in each group. Best with compact PersonCards (four, then six across beside the heading).
pairPosterCard[2]none--pair: exactly two stories as PosterCard links, 4:3 frames, the title at h3 on the scrim and the destination under the frame (Read on Northeastern Global News). One story uses MediaText; three use the default grid.
stateready | loading | emptyreadyLoading renders Skeleton cards in the slots; empty renders an EmptyState in place of the list.
bentoStoryCard[3]none--bento: the first item (__lead) takes columns 1–7 at a 4:5 frame with an h2 title; the other two stack on 8–12 at 3:2. Below 960px of the grid's width one column, the lead first at 3:2. Use it once per page to break a run of three-up rows.
staggerany[3–4]none--stagger: equal cards, every other one dropped --space-9 from 960px. For peers and people that must read as equals.
featureStoryCard[3–4]none--feature: the first item (__lead) full width as a horizontal story, photograph on columns 1–7, title from column 9; two after it sit half and half as horizontal stories, three as a 3-up row.
listStoryCard[2–5]none--list: ruled rows, a 3:2 photograph on columns 1–4 and the copy from column 5 (meta under the h3 title, never above it). When the copy should carry the section and the pictures support it.

Events

  • more The reader asked for the next set; the organism appends, keeps focus on the button, and announces the new count.

Accessibility

  • The section is labelled by its heading (aria-labelledby).
  • Cards are list items, so screen readers announce the count.
  • After Load more, focus stays on the button and the status line (a polite live region) says how many now show; the first new card is next in tab order.
  • Skeletons are aria-hidden; the list carries aria-busy="true" while loading.
  • Grouped: each group is a <section> labelled by its heading, so the office names form the page outline.
  • Pair: a story that leaves the site says so in its link text, not only with the icon.

Usage

  • Keep every card in a grid the same kind and the same image ratio.
  • Put the ArrowLink opposite the heading so it is found before the cards.
  • Bento: lead with the story with the strongest photograph, not the newest.
  • Mix stories and events in one grid.
  • Icon-plus-heading feature cards: that is not what this is for.
  • Infinite scroll in place of Load more.
  • Pair: invent a third story to fill a grid, or leave an empty third slot.
  • Bento: two on one page, or a lead without a photograph.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · ProgramCardv0.1 · 2026-11-17

ProgramCard

One card for every kind of program a student can apply to: a study-abroad program, an experiential opportunity, an entrepreneurship offering. A square-cornered photo, the title, the facts as run-in KeyValue lines, and a foot with the status Tag and an ArrowLink cue (external when it leaves for GoGlobal). Grid for browsing, row for the list view of a Finder.

Organism

Found on

Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
titletextrequiredThe program's own name: IES Abroad Vienna, Dialogue of Civilizations, Mosaic. Heading h3 at h4 size.
hrefurlrequiredOn the title link, stretched over the card. External destinations (GoGlobal, a partner site) add “, on GoGlobal” for screen readers.
imageImage 3x2placeholderalt="". With no real photo the card shows the globe on a sunken ground; never repeat one stock image across a list.
factsKeyValue run-inrequiredTwo or three, the same keys in the same order across a list: Location, Terms, Application deadline (programs); Category, Open to (opportunities).
statusTag open | closing | closednoneApplications open; Closes Jan 15 (inside 30 days); Closed. Driven by the deadline field, never typed into copy.
typeTagnoneOne neutral Tag: program type or category. Two tags at most in the foot.
cuetextView programArrowLink look, aria-hidden: names the destination (View on GoGlobal, Explore co-op). External icon when it leaves the site.
layoutgrid | rowgridRow for list view; the photo takes two ninths of the row, never under 96px.
<article class="nu-program-card">
  <span class="nu-program-card__media"><img class="nu-image nu-image--3x2" src="…" alt=""></span>
  <div class="nu-program-card__body">
    <h3 class="nu-heading nu-heading--h4 nu-program-card__title">
      <a class="nu-program-card__link" href="https://goglobal.northeastern.edu/…">IES Abroad Vienna<span class="u-vh">, on GoGlobal</span></a>
    </h3>
    <dl class="nu-key-value nu-key-value--run-in">
      <div class="nu-key-value__row"><dt>Location</dt><dd>Vienna, Austria</dd></div>
      <div class="nu-key-value__row"><dt>Terms</dt><dd>Fall, spring</dd></div>
    </dl>
    <div class="nu-program-card__foot">
      <div class="nu-program-card__tags"><span class="nu-tag nu-tag--open">…Applications open</span></div>
      <span class="nu-arrow-link nu-arrow-link--sm nu-arrow-link--external nu-program-card__cue" aria-hidden="true">View on GoGlobal …</span>
    </div>
  </div>
</article>

Events

  • click Native navigation from the title link (anywhere on the card).

Accessibility

  • One link per card: the title. Photo, facts, tags and cue are not separate tab stops.
  • Status is a word in a Tag (with an icon), never colour alone; it is read after the title.
  • Focus rings the whole card.
  • Facts are a <dl>; dates are <time datetime>.

Usage

  • Keep the fact keys identical across a list so the eye can run down a column.
  • Let closed programs stay in results, stepped back, unless the reader filters them out.
  • A program-type eyebrow above the title: the type is a Tag in the foot.
  • Rounded photos, shadows, or a box around the card.
  • A second Apply or Learn more button inside the card.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · FilterPanelv0.1 · 2026-11-17

FilterPanel

The facets of a directory as one GET form: a keyword SearchField, ChipGroups for short facets, ruled ChoiceField checkbox lists with counts for long ones, Selects for very long ones, and Clear all. A sticky sidebar from 960px; a Dialog drawer below it, opened by a Filters button that counts active filters. The applied row repeats each active value as a removable Chip above the results.

Level
Organism
Class
.nu-filter-panel __head __facet __more __clear __foot __badge __applied --sidebar
Composes
Heading, SearchField, ChipGroup, ChoiceField, Field, Select, Chip, Button, Icon, Dialog
Used by
Finder
Found on
geo G15: Browse Programs filter panel (keyword + Program Type, Country (78), Term, Field of Study (~120), City, Region, Class Type, Program Status, info tooltips, Clear All Filters); experiential #21/#22: Category / Education level / Duration checkbox dropdowns that keyboard users cannot reach; research #29: Themes (3) / Subjects (8) / Campuses (6) dropdowns, filter state only in #filter; entrepreneurship E2: four token fields, a Filter button, a Filter Results toggle on mobile

Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
facets{key, label, kind, options}[]requiredkind: chips (up to about eight short values), checkboxes (long lists, ruled, with counts), select (a hundred values or more), search.
values{[key]: value[]}{}Reflected in the URL query (?term=fall&type=study-abroad), so every filtered view can be shared and bookmarked.
counts{[key]: {[value]: number}}noneResults each value would give with the other filters applied. Counts on this sheet are illustrative; the 182 total and the experiential category counts are real.
visiblenumber6Checkbox lists show this many, then Show all N.
presentationsidebar | drawersidebarFinder chooses: sidebar from 960px, drawer (inside Dialog --drawer) below.
totalnumberrequired in drawerLabels the drawer's primary button: Show 12 opportunities.
<form class="nu-filter-panel nu-filter-panel--sidebar" method="get" action="/browse-programs/" aria-labelledby="filters-title">
  <div class="nu-filter-panel__head">
    <h2 class="nu-heading nu-heading--h4" id="filters-title">Filter programs</h2>
    <button class="nu-filter-panel__clear" type="reset">Clear all</button>
  </div>
  <div class="nu-filter-panel__facet"><div class="nu-search-field" role="search">…</div></div>
  <div class="nu-filter-panel__facet"><div class="nu-chip-group" role="group" aria-labelledby="facet-type">…</div></div>
  <fieldset class="nu-filter-panel__facet nu-choice-field nu-choice-field--ruled">
    <legend class="nu-label">Country</legend>
    <label class="nu-choice-field__option">…United Kingdom… <span class="nu-choice-field__count">9</span></label>
    <button class="nu-filter-panel__more" type="button" aria-expanded="false">Show all 78 countries …</button>
  </fieldset>
</form>

Events

  • change { key, values } on every chip, checkbox or select change; the Finder refetches and updates the count live.
  • clear { key? } from a facet's Clear all or the panel's Clear all.
  • apply Drawer only: closes the dialog and moves focus to the results heading.

Accessibility

  • One <form method="get">; every facet is a <fieldset> with a <legend> (ChoiceField) or a role="group" named by its label (ChipGroup). Real inputs throughout, so the experiential keyboard trap cannot recur.
  • The keyword field is the SearchField molecule as a div role="search", since forms cannot nest.
  • Show all is a button with aria-expanded; the extra options are already in the DOM after it.
  • Removing an applied chip says so: Remove filter: Fall.
  • Clear all is disabled, not hidden, when nothing is chosen.

Usage

  • Put the facet people use most first: status and type before country.
  • Keep zero-count values visible and disabled, so the facet keeps its shape.
  • Update results as values change on desktop; in the drawer, apply on Show N results.
  • Dropdowns of checkboxes: open lists are faster and accessible.
  • Info-icon tooltips on every facet label: write a clearer label.
  • A dark or tinted box around the panel.

<section class="nu-event-list" aria-labelledby="events-title">

    </section>

</section>

Events

  • view upcoming or past from the segment; the list reloads and the URL updates (?view=past).
  • more Load the next month; focus moves to its heading.

Accessibility

  • Month headings are real headings (h3), so the list can be scanned by heading; each event title is an h4.
  • The segment is a ChipGroup with aria-pressed, named Show.
  • Each event is one link (its title), inside a list per month so the count is announced.
  • Dates are <time datetime>; the year shows only when it is not this year.

Usage

  • Name the campus or format with a Tag on every event.
  • Keep the page title and the list in step: the geo list announced 2021 dates over 2026 events.
  • Date pickers and Today buttons for a list this short.
  • Learn more buttons inside the cards.
  • Ongoing date ranges (Sept. 1–Dec. 31) mixed into dated rows.

Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
titletextrequiredA Heading above the table, also its name (aria-labelledby); the meta line gives the row count and a standing caveat.
columns{key, label, sortable?, numeric?}[]requiredNumeric columns right-align. Labels are nouns in sentence case: NU credits, not NU CREDITS.
rowsobject[]requiredThe first cell is a row header (<th scope="row">). Cells may hold Text, Link, Tag, <abbr> codes or short rich text.
sort{key, direction}noneSets aria-sort on that head; one column at a time.
detaildialog | expand | nonenoneDialog for a record with its own facts (a course); expand for one long note under a short row (a date).
toolsslotnoneField, Select and ChoiceField filters with a Clear filters Button, above the table.
narrowwrap | wide | stackwrapUnder 720px of the table's own width: short tables wrap; --wide keeps 640px and scrolls with the first column pinned; --stack makes labelled blocks (needs data-label on every cell).
densityregular | compactregularCompact for long reference tables and short numeric ones.
stateready | loading | emptyreadyLoading keeps the head and shows Skeleton rows (aria-busy); empty shows an inline EmptyState across the columns.
<div class="nu-data-table">
  <div class="nu-data-table__head">
    <h3 class="nu-heading nu-heading--h3" id="courses">Courses at N.U.in Greece</h3>
    <p class="nu-text nu-text--meta" role="status">33 courses</p>
  </div>
  <div class="nu-data-table__scroll" role="region" aria-labelledby="courses" tabindex="0">
    <table aria-labelledby="courses">
      <thead><tr>
        <th scope="col" aria-sort="ascending"><button class="nu-data-table__sort" type="button">Course <svg class="nu-icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-sort"></use></svg><svg class="nu-icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-chevron-down"></use></svg></button></th>
        <th scope="col" class="nu-data-table__num">NU credits</th>
      </tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr>
          <th scope="row"><button class="nu-data-table__open" type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog"><span class="nu-data-table__code">HIS 232</span>Thessaloniki: A City and Its Inhabitants</button></th>
          <td class="nu-data-table__num">4.00</td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</div>

Events

  • sort { key, direction } from a head button; the organism reorders rows and moves aria-sort.
  • open { row } from a row button; the page opens the Dialog with that record.
  • toggle { row, expanded } from a row's chevron.
  • filter { facet, values } from the tools; the row count in the head is a live region.

Accessibility

  • A real <table> with <th scope="col"> and <th scope="row">; never a grid of divs.
  • Sort is a <button> inside the head cell; the cell carries aria-sort, so the state is read with the column name.
  • The scroll box is a focusable role="region" named by the title, so keyboard users can scroll it.
  • Row toggles are IconButtons with aria-expanded and aria-controls, named after the row (Show details: ACT Family Day).
  • Codes such as NUpath use <abbr title> the first time; colour never carries meaning (culture courses are a Tag, not a purple row).

Usage

  • Sort numbers as numbers and lists as people expect them (majors alphabetically, not 1., 10., 100.).
  • Right-align figures and keep their units in the head or the cell, consistently.
  • Put caveats in the meta line or the foot, once.
  • Zebra stripes, tinted first columns, or coloured rows.
  • Tables for layout or for a single callout (nuin's one-row Save the Date table is a Notice).
  • Hide columns that phones need; pin the first column or stack the rows.

Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
facetsFilterPanelrequiredThe panel's facets and their counts.
resultsProgramCard[] | LinkRow[]requiredOne kind per Finder. Grid view uses ProgramCards; list view uses ProgramCard rows or LinkRows.
total / rangeinteger, {from, to}requiredFor the ListToolbar count (role="status"), with the list's own noun: 182 programs, 12 opportunities.
sortSelect optionsnoneTwo to four orders in the toolbar; in the drawer on phones.
viewgrid | listgridThe toolbar's view chips; remembered per visitor.
pagingpages | morepagesPagination when people return to a position (programs); Load more for browsing short lists (opportunities, institutes).

<section class="nu-finder" aria-labelledby="finder-title">
  <h2 class="u-vh" id="finder-title">Programs</h2>
  <div class="nu-finder__layout">
    <aside class="nu-finder__aside" aria-label="Filters">
      <form class="nu-filter-panel nu-filter-panel--sidebar" method="get">…</form>
    </aside>
    <div class="nu-finder__main">
      <div class="nu-finder__bar nu-finder__filters"><button class="nu-button nu-button--outline nu-button--sm" type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog">… Filters</button></div>
      <div class="nu-list-toolbar">…<p class="nu-list-toolbar__count" role="status">Showing <b>1–12</b> of <b>182</b> programs</p>…</div>
      <ul class="nu-filter-panel__applied" aria-label="Applied filters">…</ul>
      <ul class="nu-finder__results" role="list" aria-label="Programs">
        <li><article class="nu-program-card">…</article></li>
      </ul>
      <div class="nu-finder__foot"><nav class="nu-pagination" aria-label="Pagination">…</nav></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <dialog class="nu-dialog nu-dialog--drawer">…the same FilterPanel…</dialog>
</section>

Events

  • query { q, facets, sort, page } whenever anything changes; the Finder writes it to the URL (?type=study-abroad&term=fall&paged=2) and fetches.
  • view grid or list.
  • more Load the next set; focus stays on the button and the count updates.

Accessibility

  • The count in the ListToolbar is the live region: “Showing 1–6 of 12 opportunities” is announced after each change, once, not per keystroke.
  • Every view is a URL, so filters, pages and sorts can be shared, bookmarked and used without script (GET form, real links).
  • After Pagination, focus moves to the results heading; after Load more, it stays on the button.
  • On phones the Filters button names how many are active (Filters, 2 active) and opens the Dialog drawer; Show N results closes it and returns focus to the results.

Usage

  • Name the noun everywhere: programs, opportunities, institutes; never “No programs found” on an institutes list.
  • Keep closed programs in results by default and let the status facet remove them.
  • Load results by AJAX with no loading or empty state (the geo staff grid sat blank).
  • Filter state that lives only in #filter.
  • Hide the total, or replace it with Page 1 of 16.

  </div>

<!-- opener: document.getElementById('course-dialog').showModal() -->

Events

  • close Native close from the × button (<form method="dialog">), Escape, or an action; returnValue names which.
  • step { direction } from previous/next; the table opens the neighbouring row.

Accessibility

  • Opened with showModal(): focus moves to the dialog, Tab stays inside, Escape closes, and the page behind is inert. No hand-rolled focus trap.
  • aria-labelledby points at the title; the close IconButton is named Close course details.
  • On close, focus returns to the control that opened it.
  • Entry is 350ms fade and 12px rise; exit 200ms; reduced motion shows and hides it at once.

Usage

  • Use it for detail that belongs to a row the reader will come back to (a course in a curriculum), or for filters on a phone.
  • Keep the actions to the step the reader takes next.
  • Open one on page load, for a newsletter, or to confirm something that can be undone.
  • Glass or blur behind it: the scrim does that job on Canvas and Night.
  • A red close button, or more than one primary action.

Canvas · light

Grouped FAQ · one item open · foot

Course selection and registration FAQs

Answers for admitted N.U.in students choosing a location and fall courses.

Location selection

How do I find out which N.U.in location is the best academic fit for me?

Your Application Status Check and Location Selection portal shows each N.U.in location matched to your major and college. If a location isn’t listed, the courses you need aren’t part of that partner school’s curriculum.

How does Northeastern decide which locations I am eligible for?

Compatibility is based on your major, age and other factors.

How will the courses appear on my transcript?

Your N.U.in courses and letter grades appear directly on your Northeastern transcript and count toward your GPA.

Course selection and registration

Why are some or most of my classes already selected for me?

Many first-year programs of study have a prescribed curriculum.

Once I choose my courses, are my selections final?

No. You’ll adjust them with your home college advising office from mid-June through July.

What is NUpath, and which ones should I pick this fall?

NUpath is Northeastern’s core curriculum, fulfilled through major and elective courses.

Events

  • toggleall { expanded } from the Expand all button; it sets open on every item.
  • toggle Native, from each item.

Accessibility

  • Each item is a native details element: keyboard and state come free and work without JavaScript; Expand all is added by script, so it is absent when script is.
  • The toggle is a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls listing the items; its label changes with its state.
  • Headings keep the outline: the section h2, group h3s, question h4s inside the summaries.
  • A URL hash naming an item (#faq-deposit) opens it and scrolls to it.

Usage

  • Group questions by the reader’s task, not the office’s org chart.
  • Close the FAQ with when it was last updated.
  • Eyebrow labels as group names (FORMAT AND LOGISTICS); use real headings.
  • Hide deadlines or eligibility inside a closed item.
  • Accordions inside accordions.

Canvas · light

Line tabs · Eligibility selected

Eligibility and policies

Academic, financial and disciplinary standing

Every program and partner institution sets its own admission criteria, but Northeastern students meet one institutional standard before they study abroad for credit.

  • Complete at least two semesters at a Northeastern campus.
  • Be enrolled in classes or co-op the term before you go.
  • Hold a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5 and meet your program’s own requirements.
  • Clear any balance on your Northeastern account before departure.

Withdrawal policies for global experience programs supersede the university’s on-campus policies.

Approved courses transfer back with a letter grade and count toward your GPA.

Colleges may limit which courses you can take abroad.

Line tabs · hover on Grading policy, last tab disabled

Application timeline

Fall applications open in early January and are due March 1 at 11:59 p.m. ET.

Spring applications open in early July and are due October 1 at 11:59 p.m. ET.

Summer applications open in early January and are due March 1 at 11:59 p.m. ET.

    <button class="nu-tabs__tab" role="tab" type="button" id="tab-withdrawal" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="panel-withdrawal" tabindex="-1">Withdrawal policy</button>

<!-- segmented: <div class="nu-tabs nu-tabs--segmented"> with <button class="nu-chip" role="tab" aria-selected="…"> -->

Events

  • change { id } when the selected tab changes (click, arrow keys, Home, End).

Accessibility

  • role="tablist" holds role="tab" buttons with aria-selected and aria-controls; panels are role="tabpanel" with aria-labelledby and hidden when inactive.
  • Roving tabindex: only the selected tab is in the tab order; arrow keys move between tabs and select them, Home and End jump to the ends.
  • Each panel takes tabindex="0" so its content is reachable even when it starts with plain text.
  • Without JavaScript, every panel shows in order under its own heading.

Usage

  • Use tabs when readers want one of several parallel answers (one term, one policy).
  • Keep panels about the same length so the page doesn’t jump.
  • Tabs for steps in a sequence (use Steps) or for content everyone must read (use Prose).
  • More than one row of tabs, or tabs inside tabs.
  • A red label or a red underline on Night.

Events

Canvas · light

Columns · five steps · call to action

How to apply

Studying abroad takes two applications: the GEO application and the host institution’s.

  1. 1

    Complete the GEO application

    Choose Apply now on your program’s brochure page, with your transcript and passport details.

  2. 2

    Get GEO approval

    Your Study Abroad Advisor reviews your application and confirms you are eligible.

  3. 3

    Apply to the host institution

    Your advisor sends instructions for the host application or nominates you directly.

  4. 4

    Receive a decision

    The host institution reviews your application and makes the acceptance decision.

  5. 5

    Finish your requirements

    GEO and the host share the last steps before you go.

Browse programs

Fall and summer applications are due March 1; spring applications are due October 1.

Rows · head beside · step 5 is current (semifinal review)

How it works

Applications for the 2026 Next Up Founders Prize are closed. The Reading Committee is reviewing every entry.

  1. 1

    Complete the eligibility form

    Share your name, date of birth, country and parent or guardian contact information so we can confirm you’re eligible.

  2. 2

    Confirm your consent form

    Every entrant signs a consent form agreeing to the contest rules. If you’re under 18, it goes to your parent or guardian.

  3. 3

    Complete your application

    We email the full application: your school and contact details, the problem you’re solving, your idea and your AI angle.

  4. 4

    Submit your video pitch

    Upload a video pitching your idea with your written answers.

  5. 5

    Advance to the semifinals, then pitch in Boston

    The Reading Committee reviews every application in a virtual semifinal round. Finalists pitch on the Boston campus during Global Entrepreneurship Week, or by video.

Full program rules and conditions

headingtextrequiredThe prompt, as an H2 (the page owns the H1). Sentence case, a promise not a label: Let’s partner to find solutions together.

<form class="nu-form nu-form--split" action="/partnerships/employer/" method="post" novalidate>
  <div class="nu-form__head">
    <h2 class="nu-heading nu-heading--h2">Let’s partner to find solutions to your challenges together.</h2>
    <p class="nu-form__note">Fields marked (required) must be filled in.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="nu-form__body">
    <!-- on a failed submit: <div class="nu-notice nu-notice--error" role="alert" tabindex="-1">… <ul class="nu-form__errors"><li><a class="nu-link" href="#email">…</a></li></ul></div> -->
    <fieldset class="nu-form__group">
      <legend>About you</legend>
      <div class="nu-form__row"><div class="nu-field">…</div><div class="nu-field">…</div></div>
    </fieldset>
    <div class="nu-form__foot">
      <div class="nu-choice-field">…</div>
      <div class="nu-form__actions">
        <button class="nu-button nu-button--accent" type="submit">Send inquiry</button>
        <p class="nu-form__note">The partnerships team replies within two business days.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</form>

Events

  • submit { fields } after client validation passes; the page posts it and sets busy.
  • invalid { errors: [{ id, message }] }: the page renders the summary and moves focus to it.

Accessibility

  • Validate on blur and on submit, never per keystroke. On a failed submit, move focus to the summary (tabindex="-1"), whose links jump to each field.
  • The summary is role="alert"; each field keeps its own ErrorText joined by aria-describedby, so the problem is read at the field too.
  • Required is said in words: (required) on the label, and the note in the head explains it once.
  • While sending, the button keeps its accessible name with aria-busy="true"; the success Notice is role="status" and takes focus.
  • Works without JavaScript: a real <form action> posts and the server returns the same states.

Usage

  • Ask only what the office will use; every field costs completions.
  • Write the promise beside the button: when the reply comes and from whom.
  • Keep the reader’s answers after an error.
  • Placeholder text as labels, or a CAPTCHA puzzle before submit.
  • A red border with no words, or errors only at the top.
  • Clear the form on error or hide it after success without saying what happens next.

Canvas · light

Facet page: sections, run-in paragraph, inline FileLink, list, table, aside

Pre-departure orientation

To help you prepare for your fall semester, The N.U.in Program hosts Pre-Departure Orientation in the summer before you leave. Review the N.U.in Orientation page for dates and attendance requirements.

What to pack

For a suggested packing list, read the N.U.in packing guide (PDF). Whatever you pack, you will carry, on planes, trains and buses.

Adapters and voltage converters: the electricity supply in Greece runs at 220–240 volts and 50 hertz. Check that your devices are compatible before you bring them; hair straighteners and blow dryers may need a converter.

Group flight

The N.U.in Program fee includes a group flight to and from your location, with transportation between the airport and your residence. Registration opens in late spring or early summer through Application Status Check.

If you opt out of the group flight

  • Book your own flight. You arrange your own itinerary.
  • Arrive on the start date. Early check-in is not available.
  • Get yourself to the residence. You arrange travel from the airport at the start of the program.

Students on the group flight depart together from the United States. Outbound changes are not permitted; some airlines allow changes to return flights.

Important dates

Key dates for the N.U.in Greece fall 2026 semester. Program dates are subject to change.

Story, large: paragraphs, blockquote with cite, subhead

Rachel Rodgers, associate professor in the Department of Applied Psychology, directs the Applied Psychology Program in Appearance and Eating Research (APPEAR) Lab. She works to characterize the relationship between social media use and body image, which means refining the tools that measure what social media does to the people who use it.

The way someone feels about their body on a given day shapes how they use social media: how long they hover over a post, whether they watch a full video, whether they follow a profile. Those choices shape what the algorithm shows them next.

“Before deciding how we intervene, I think we really need to understand it all.”

Rachel Rodgers, associate professor of applied psychology

Body image and identity

This research fits into Rodgers’ larger focus on how appearance serves economic and political goals. The “trending” appearance, she says, is usually one only people with the social and financial resources to pursue it can reach.

FAQ answer: list, figure, last updated

How should a shared research facility set charges for users?

Set user fees from actual costs and actual use. The administrative guidelines describe the rate setup in full; the basic principles are:

  1. Federally sponsored users always get the lowest rate.
  2. A facility recovers only the cost of operating it.
  3. External users may be charged higher rates that include the facility’s F&A costs.

Last updated on May 15, 2024

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
contentHTMLrequiredWhatever the editor wrote: p, h2–h4, ul, ol, dl, blockquote (with cite), figure (img + figcaption, or table), table, hr, aside, a, strong, em, small.

<div class="nu-prose">
  <!-- raw CMS HTML, no classes needed -->
  <h2>Group flight</h2>

  <ul><li><strong>Book your own flight.</strong> You arrange your own itinerary.</li></ul>

Events

  • None. Presentational only.

Accessibility

  • The page outline continues into the body: the page’s H1 lives in the header, so prose starts at h2. Empty CMS headings are hidden, not read.
  • Links are underlined at rest; phone numbers are tel: links.
  • Tables keep <th scope> and a <caption> or a heading before them; the table’s figure scrolls sideways on phones instead of squeezing.
  • Blockquotes carry the speaker in <cite>; a pull quote that repeats the text is aria-hidden in the CMS block.

Usage

  • Let editors write semantic HTML and nothing else: the region does the styling.
  • Use a definition list for run-in labels (Meals, Laundry, Mail) so they read as pairs.
  • Close policy and FAQ pages with the last-updated line.
  • Spacer headings, <br> stacks or &nbsp; for space.
  • Coloured, bold, underlined links (nuin’s red), or italics for whole paragraphs.
  • Tables for layout or for a one-row callout: that is a Notice.

Events

  • None. Presentational only.

Accessibility

  • Every email and phone value is a mailto: or tel: link with the full international number in href.
  • Addresses are <address>; hours carry their time zone.
  • The emergency mark is decorative; the heading says Emergency in words.
  • People rows are a list, so screen readers announce how many.

Usage

  • Write hours with the time zone: Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m. ET.
  • Put the emergency block where people look first on safety pages, and repeat it in the footer of travel content.
  • Emails and phone numbers as plain text.
  • A red box or red numbers for emergencies, or a boxed card for an ordinary office.

Events

  • click Native navigation on each pill (Apply, Request information and Visit open the admissions forms).

Accessibility

  • A <section> named by its heading (aria-labelledby), so it is a landmark screen-reader users can jump to.
  • The pills are links (<a class="nu-button">): they go to pages, they do not act on this one.
  • Every pill is 48px tall; on phones they stack full width.
  • Red appears only as the Apply fill under white text (5.9:1 on Night).

Usage

  • Keep the three actions in this order on every page so they become muscle memory.
  • Use the same copy sitewide; a unit may swap the sentence, never the actions' order.
  • A photograph behind it, or a wordmark image above it (the footer already carries the lockup).
  • An eyebrow such as “Take action” over the heading.
  • More than one accent pill, or arrows on the pills.

  • click Native navigation; the whole row is the link.

Accessibility

  • A real <ul> of links: screen readers hear “list, 4 items” and each link's name and description.

  • Section numbers before the names.
  • Centre the list: the ragged left edge of display type is the design.

  • A <ul> of links: screen readers hear the count, then each title and description as one link.

  • A button inside a tile: the tile is the link.
  • Five or more tiles: use PathwayList (md) or a CardGrid.
  • Mix tiles with and without descriptions, or with and without photographs.

Canvas · light

Numbered, with its own heading · Experiential learning defined: how experiential learning benefits you

How experiential learning benefits you

  1. Test career paths in real settings

    Earn income through paid co-op positions, while exploring career paths before committing to one.

  2. Graduate with substantial work experience

    Complete 6–18 months of professional work, not just summer internships.

  3. Build a global professional network

    Work with employers and mentors at one or more of our 4,000+ partner organizations across seven continents.

  4. Develop practical skills

    Apply your coursework to real projects, from conducting clinical research to exploring how AI can help accelerate breakthroughs on pressing problems.

  5. Strengthen professional skills

    Learn to communicate with clients, collaborate across teams, navigate workplace dynamics and adapt to different organizational cultures.

  6. Compete with confidence

    Join the 90%+ of graduates who secure jobs or graduate school admission within 9 months.

  7. Drive responsible innovation

    Play a role in shaping how emerging technologies like AI drive experimentation, ethical use and thoughtful integration across the university.

Events

  • None. Presentational only.

Accessibility

  • A real <ul> or <ol>; numbers are the list's own order (generated), so screen readers do not hear them twice.
  • Claims are headings (h3 under the section's h2, set at h4 size) so the list can be skimmed by heading.
  • The heading's stickiness never covers the rows: it sits in its own columns.

Usage

  • Split run-in bullets into claim and sentence: the claim is what the eye scans.
  • Put a photograph above the list, full-bleed, if the section needs one; never beside it.
  • Bold run-in terms inside a bullet paragraph.
  • Icons or numbers in circles before the claims.
  • Use it for a sequence the reader must follow: that is Steps.

I. General privacy policy scope

This general Privacy Policy describes how Northeastern collects and handles Personal Information through your use of our Sites and Apps and in support of our Operations. It also describes your privacy rights and choices and our privacy practices when processing personal information for these purposes.

For more information about this Privacy Policy and your rights under applicable law, please contact us at privacy@northeastern.edu.

II. What information do we collect?

We collect Personal Information that you voluntarily give us when you visit the Sites, Apps or we engage with you through our Operations, such as marketing, fundraising, and IT. This information includes:

  • Name, title, age, and date of birth
  • Contact information including address, city, state, postal code, country of residence, email address, home, cellular and other contact telephone number(s)
  • Attendance at Northeastern University events
  • Records of communications between you and the University

Automatically collected data

When you use the Sites and Apps, information including the following may be created and automatically logged in our systems.

  • Frame a logo inside a framed tile.
  • Float the industry tag to the row's far edge, away from the name.
  • Full-colour logos at rest.

    <div class="nu-gallery__title">
      <h2 class="nu-heading nu-heading--h2" id="gls-photos">Conversations and candid moments</h2>

  </header>

        <button class="nu-gallery__open" type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-label="Open photo 1 of 60">
          <img class="nu-image nu-image--3x2" src="…" alt="…"></button>

      </figure>
      …

<dialog class="nu-gallery__viewer" data-mode="dark" aria-label="Photo viewer">…</dialog>

Events

  • open A photo (or View all) was chosen: the page calls showModal() on the viewer at that index.
  • step Previous or next, also bound to the arrow keys while the viewer is open.
  • close Close, Esc, or a click on the backdrop; focus returns to the photo that opened it.

Accessibility

  • Each photo is a <button aria-haspopup="dialog"> named “Open photo 3 of 60”; the image keeps its alt text.
  • The viewer is a native modal <dialog> named “Photo viewer”: focus is trapped and Esc closes it.
  • Close, Previous photo and Next photo are labelled IconButtons; at the first and last photo the step is disabled.
  • The count is a live region (aria-live="polite") so stepping announces “9 of 60”.
  • On phones captions leave the grid but stay in the markup for screen readers, and appear in the viewer.

Usage

  • Lead with the strongest frame; mix a portrait crop into every justified row so the rhythm breathes.
  • Credit staff photography in the viewer caption.
  • Dot pagination for 60 photos: show nine and View all.
  • Rounded tiles, drop shadows or a white mat around the photos.
  • Autoplay the viewer as a slideshow.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · PosterRailv0.1 · 2026-11-17

PosterRail

A workhorse. A set of parallel items as tall posters in one rail that starts on the content edge and runs off the right edge of the window. Use it in place of a row of equal cards when there are five to twelve things of one kind that are browsed, not scanned by name. Each poster is one link named by its title (an h3) that reads title, meta, text, cue under a 4:5 picture, on shared lines across the row. It is the shared rail (a progress line that follows the scroll, a count of the posters in view, paddles that disable at the ends, 1:1 mouse drag) and the worked example of a section pattern in docs/BUILDER-GUIDE.md. Four across from 960px with the fifth in the margin; one and a third on phones.

Events

  • page A paddle scrolls to the next or previous screenful, landing on an item's edge; each paddle disables at its end.
  • drag Mouse drag scrolls the rail 1:1; on release it settles on the nearest item. The click that ends a drag is swallowed.
  • click Each item's navigation.

Accessibility

  • The rail is a list of links; Tab moves through them and scrolls each into view (the focus ring stands outside the card at the system offset: the track keeps a step of room above and below). Swipe, wheel and trackpad scroll it natively.
  • Paddles are real buttons named for what they page; a paddle that reaches its end while focused stays focusable and says aria-disabled, so the keyboard never drops out.
  • The progress line is decorative (aria-hidden) and follows the scroll itself; beside it the count says which items are in view of how many (1–3 of 10).
  • An item that takes the keyboard's focus while cut off by either edge is brought wholly into view. Controls show only when the rail can travel at least one item's width.
  • With a mouse the track shows the grab cursor wherever it is not a link; a drag never opens the card under the pointer.
  • Nothing moves by itself. Reduced motion: paddles jump instead of gliding, and the progress line is set when the scroll comes to rest instead of travelling with it. On paper the rail prints as a grid of every item.
  • Each poster is one link named by its title (the picture's alt is empty unless it adds something).

Usage

  • Use pictures of one shape and similar weight; the row reads as a set.
  • Keep titles to two lines at 288px.
  • Fewer than four posters (use a pair or a MediaText) or more than eight (link to the index).
  • An auto-advancing row.
  • A kicker above a poster's title: a category goes under it as meta.

  • click Opens the publication (the title link, stretched over the item).

  • A double rule: the list brings its own hairlines, so no heavy label rule under a hero rule.

Northeastern Design System · Organism · StageTabsv0.1 · 2026-11-17

StageTabs

A workhorse. Two to six parallel items as one large stage and a row of pill tabs that swaps it: each item brings a picture or film and one block of copy (title, text, pill, never split). Use it where a row of three equal cards would otherwise sit and each item deserves a full-size picture. One marker glides between the pills; the stage cross-fades and keeps the tallest panel's height. Without script the pills are links and the panels read stacked. Phones: the pills wrap onto as many lines as they need, so every name stays in view; the picture stacks over the copy and the stage is as tall as the panel showing. --titles (the helper's tabs set to titles) drops the pills: every panel's own title shows at once as a ruled list beside the stage that never moves, the current one's text and action in one slot under the list (phones: the list, the picture, the text). --large (size="large"): the panel's title at the section heading's size, and with --media-2 the portrait on three columns and the copy on nine. When not to use tabs: two items (MediaText, OffsetPair); items with no pictures, or more than six (IndexRows); anything the reader must see without a click, and three short items, where tabs of any kind hide two-thirds of the content (MixedRail, UnevenGrid).

<!-- with script: role="tablist" / role="tab" aria-selected / role="tabpanel" inert.
     meta and blocks: <div class="nu-tabs__lead"><div class="nu-tabs__text"><p class="nu-text nu-text--meta">…</p><p class="nu-text">…</p>
       <ul class="nu-tabs__points" role="list"><li class="nu-text">…</li></ul></div><div class="nu-tabs__actions">pill, ArrowLinks</div></div>
     tabs="titles": class="… nu-tabs--titles" data-dx-stage-tabs="titles", no __controls, titles at nu-heading--h4; with script each title
       holds <button type="button" class="nu-tabs__pick" aria-expanded>, each __copy and its __title carry aria-current, the
       __title data-hover and data-hover-line, and the other panels' __media and __lead are inert. -->

Events

  • select A tab is chosen (click, arrow keys, Home, End, or an address ending in the panel's id). The script moves aria-selected, marks the other panels inert, points the marker at the pill and writes the panel's id to the address.
  • click The panel's pill navigates.

Accessibility

  • With script the row is a tablist: one tab stop, arrow keys move and select (and wrap), Home and End jump, Space selects; each panel is a tabpanel labelled by its tab, and panels that are not showing are inert.
  • Without script the pills are in-page links and every panel is visible in order.
  • The selected pill is marked by aria-selected and by the one filled marker; hover, focus and press are the Chip's own.
  • --titles: each title is a button inside its h3 (aria-expanded); the open row's button is aria-disabled because one row is always open; the other rows' text and pictures are inert.
  • A film (the FilmPlayer) plays muted only while its panel is showing and in view, has a pause control on the picture's lower left, and stays on its poster under reduced motion.
  • Reduced motion: the panels swap and the marker jumps, with no fade or travel.
  • The stage holds its tallest panel at every width (--titles: the titles never move and the text slot is as tall as the longest row's text), so nothing below it moves when a tab changes.
  • Text in a panel that is not showing is out of reach of find-in-page (it is inert); where every word must be findable use IndexRows --disclose. On paper every panel prints, in order.

Usage

  • Give every panel a picture of the same shape and similar weight.
  • Keep the panels' copy about the same length: the stage is as tall as the longest.
  • Keep labels to one to three words so the row fits one line at 1440 (on phones the pills wrap onto as many lines as they need).
  • Use --tabs-start whenever the header is not centred.
  • More than six items, or items without pictures (use IndexRows).
  • Two items (use MediaText twice, or OffsetPair).
  • Auto-advance the tabs.
  • Put the only copy of important text in a later panel if the page depends on it being seen.
  • A panel title larger than the section heading: size="large" stops at h2.
  • Tabs over three short items: two-thirds of the content would wait behind a click (use UnevenGrid or MixedRail).

Northeastern Design System · Organism · StickyScenesv0.1 · 2026-11-17

StickyScenes

A workhorse (compact chapters). Three to five short chapters of copy scroll past one picture frame that stays put and cross-fades to each chapter's picture; a line under the frame, cut into one segment per chapter, carries one mark that glides to the chapter showing. Chapters sit one step apart, so two share the window with the frame and the section costs about a sixth of a window per chapter. The section is never shorter than the frame plus one step, so the frame always pins. Native scroll and position:sticky only. Without script each chapter is its picture beside its copy. Phones: the chapters are cards in one sideways row (picture, caption, copy; the next card at the edge), about one screen high; --phones-stack stacks them instead; nothing is pinned.

Level
Organism
Section pattern
Workhorse: conventional reading order, efficient with height; use as often as the page needs.
