Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
headingSectionHeaderrequiredAny variant, at h2. The stage follows one --head-gap below.
items3–5 × { title, text?, link?, media, meta?, caption? }requiredtitle is an h3 at h3 size. meta is one small line under it (a role, a placement). text is a paragraph or a list of blocks (paragraphs, ruled lists). link is an ArrowLink, or a list of them. media is one Image; pinned, it fills a five-column landscape frame (at most 448px tall, never taller than the window). caption is a short line about the picture itself (who, where; three lines at most), set small: it always stays with its own picture: under the pinned frame and its mark while that picture shows (--captions), under each picture where nothing is pinned.
reversebooleanfalseFrame on the right, copy on the left (--reverse).
ratio3x2 | 4x5 | 1x1 | 16x93x2The pictures' shape where nothing is pinned. Pinned, the frame is the five-column landscape, which 3x2 and 16x9 pictures fill; with 4x5 or 1x1 (--ratio-…) the pinned frame takes that shape too, as wide as five columns or as the window's height allows, and the mark and caption keep its width. A portrait frame is taller than two short chapters: give it three or more.
stepcompactunset (352px)--step-compact: 224px a chapter, for a title and two or three lines. At any step the stage is at least the frame plus one step, so the frame always pins for at least one step.
phonesrail | stackrailUnder 720px. rail: the chapters are cards in one sideways row (native scroll and snap, no controls), the next card showing at the edge. stack (--phones-stack): each chapter's picture, then its copy, down the page.
gaptight | standard | chapterstandardThe section's seam above, on the wrapper (nu-section--…). The page chooses it.
groundCanvas | NightCanvasdata-mode="dark" on the wrapper for Night.
<section class="nu-section nu-sticky-scenes" aria-labelledby="h" data-dx-sticky-scenes>
  <header class="nu-section-header" data-reveal>…</header>
  <div class="nu-sticky-scenes__stage">
    <ol class="nu-sticky-scenes__items" role="list">
      <li class="nu-sticky-scenes__item">   <!-- the script sets aria-current="true" on the chapter in view -->
        <figure class="nu-sticky-scenes__media" data-drift="soft" data-reveal="unmask"><img class="nu-image nu-image--3x2" src="…" alt=""></figure>
        <p class="nu-text nu-text--small nu-sticky-scenes__caption">…</p>   <!-- optional: a line about the picture; the wrapper then carries nu-sticky-scenes--captions -->
        <div class="nu-sticky-scenes__copy">
          <h3 class="nu-heading nu-heading--h3 nu-sticky-scenes__title">Faculty</h3>
          <p class="nu-text">…</p>
          <a class="nu-arrow-link" href="…">Learn more </a>
        </div>
      </li>
      …
    </ol>
    <span class="nu-sticky-scenes__progress" style="--count:3" aria-hidden="true" data-indicator="line"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
  </div>
</section>

Events

  • scene The chapter whose first line has passed the middle of the window becomes current: aria-current="true" on its item; the mark (data-indicator="line") glides to its segment. An IntersectionObserver reports it: nothing runs while the page scrolls.

Accessibility

  • The chapters are an ordered list in the document, each with its own picture; nothing is hidden from assistive technology.
  • Scrolling is native: no wheel or touch handling, no snapping. A jump (an anchor, Home, End) lands on the right scene.
  • The frame pins under everything the page pins: the unit bar and any travelling bar (--pin-top). Focus inside a chapter makes it the chapter showing.
  • Chapters that are not showing step back to the muted ink, which still passes AA.
  • Motion: the pictures cross-fade (nothing slides or scales), drift softly inside the frame as it enters and leaves, and the frame unmasks once. Reduced motion: the pictures swap, nothing else moves.
  • The progress line is decorative (aria-hidden); the list order carries the sequence.

Usage

  • Use landscape pictures for the default frame (about 5:4 at 1440, square near 1024); pass ratio for uprights and squares.
  • Keep each chapter to a heading, two to four lines and one link. Each holds one step (352px; 224px with step="compact") so its picture has its moment.
  • Let it be the one pinned sequence on a page.
  • More than five chapters: the reader is held too long.
  • Chapters of a line or two, or only two chapters: the frame barely pins; use StageTabs tabs="titles".
  • Text set on the pictures: a caption goes under the frame.
  • Put it directly after another pinned pattern.

Northeastern Design System · Organism · IndexRowsv0.1 · 2026-11-17

IndexRows

A workhorse. Five to fourteen parallel items as an index of ruled rows in place of a wall of equal cards. Default: every row is one link with its title at h3 size (and an optional sentence under it), and the row under the pointer or the keyboard (on touch, the row crossing the middle of the window) calls its picture into a 4:5 frame pinned beside the list while the other rows step back; wherever the frame does not show, each row carries a small thumbnail instead. --disclose: an accordion of native <details> whose rows open independently; the meta stands beside the title on its baseline; an open row is a small designed panel sized to its content: with a landscape picture, the text and link on the measure (five columns) and the picture on the last six at its own shape; with a portrait or square (--portrait), a portrait on three columns (two with --portrait-sm) under the name and the text beside it on the measure. Phones and touch: the pinned frame goes and the thumbnails carry the pictures; in the accordion the picture closes the open row.

Level
Organism
Section pattern
Workhorse: conventional reading order, efficient with height; use as often as the page needs.

Events

  • choose Default form: pointer over a row, or focus on it, moves aria-current to that row's picture in the frame; the other rows step back (data-hover-group).
  • toggle Disclose form: the browser's own <details> toggle; rows open independently (with exclusive, opening one closes the others through name). The height opens smoothly and the sign turns from plus to minus (data-disclose, data-disclose-sign).
  • click A row's or a panel's link navigates.

Accessibility

  • Every row is a real link (or a real <summary>); Tab walks them in order and focus shows the same state as the pointer.
  • Row titles are h3 elements. Every row is the same height (the first included). The pinned frame is decorative (aria-hidden): the thumbnails carry the alt text and show wherever the frame does not. It pins under everything the page pins (--pin-top).
  • The accordion works without script, with the keyboard and with find-in-page; opening glides where the browser can interpolate to auto, and simply opens elsewhere. A row opens when the address names it, its title (<hid>-row-<n>) or anything in it; a long open row keeps its summary in view; every row prints open (the shared disclosure).
  • Panel links are 44px targets.
  • Reduced motion: pictures swap and rows open without animation.

Usage

  • Give every row a picture of similar weight; the frame crops to 4:5.
  • Use --disclose when each item has a sentence and a link.
  • Fewer than five rows in the default form (use UnevenGrid or StageTabs).
  • A row that is only a name when the reader has to choose between rows: give it its meta, its sentence (text) or, in --disclose, its line.
  • A paragraph in a row of the default form: one sentence at most.
  • Show the thumbnails and the frame together.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · PillarIndexv0.1 · 2026-11-17

PillarIndex

The brand pillars as doors to their own pages: one row per pillar on full-width hairlines, the pillar's name in Light at h2 size, its theme line and a cue naming the destination. From 960px a 4:5 photograph stands beside the rows, the first pillar's until the reader points at another, with a caption saying what the picture shows; phones keep each picture as a square thumbnail beside its name. For three to six doors that each deserve a sentence and a picture (About's five pillars); for audience doors set as type alone use PathwayList, for two to four child pages PathwayCards.

Northeastern Design System · Organism · NameWallv0.1 · 2026-11-17

NameWall

A set of places or things by name (the campuses), each name a link that calls up its photograph and one line about it. One name is always current. Default, a workhorse: a list of names at heading size with the place beside each, and one pinned picture with the current name and its sentence as the caption over it, always in the window with the name in hand (h2 in one column up to eight names; h3 in two columns beyond that). Statements, opt-in: --display sets the names in two even columns at h1 (the largest size that keeps the longest name on one line in four columns); --contained is the Night wall and the recommended statement (names in two even columns at h2 on eight columns beside a pinned square frame, about one window high, no picture past its own pixels); --backdrop is the full-bleed photograph behind the wall, only for pictures of 1920 × 1080 or more (the helper builds --contained otherwise). No picture is ever shown past its own pixels: the helper reads the files and steps the frame down. From 720 to 960px, and without script from 720px, every form is a plain ruled list: each name with its place, a small picture and its sentence. Phones (under 720px), by default: the current name's picture once under the heading, then the names as ruled rows of 48px or more, each one link with its place, two columns from nine names (about one screen for ten to fourteen names; the sentences stay each link's description); --phones-list keeps the long list, --phones-rail makes the names a sideways row of cards. Pointer and keyboard choose a name from 960px; on touch there the name crossing the middle of the window becomes current as the reader scrolls.

Level
Organism
Section pattern
Workhorse: conventional reading order, efficient with height; use as often as the page needs.

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
headingSectionHeaderrequiredAny variant, at h2. In --backdrop it sits on the photograph: pass the heading alone, no lead.
items5–14 × { name, url, place?, image, alt, text?, focus? }requiredplace is set small after the name. text is the one sentence shown with the picture, at reading size (the caption, after the name: on the frame over the picture, or under the names across their columns where the names end well above the picture's foot: the two-column list and a contained wall of twelve names or fewer, --caption-under, set by the helper; on glass in --backdrop; under the name in the list form); each link is described by it. focus is the picture's object-position.
sizeh2 | displayh2h2: the list (names at h2, or at h3 in two columns when there are more than eight: --cols-2). display: a statement, the names in two even columns at h1, each place under its name (--display).
backdropfalse | contained | truefalseThe Night statement. contained (--contained): the names in two even columns at h2 on eight columns beside a pinned square frame, about one window high. true (--backdrop): full bleed, ONLY when every picture is 1920 × 1080 or more (the wrapper carries data-mode="dark", nu-section--flush and nu-section--bleed, two Scrims over the photograph, the caption on glass beside the names); with smaller pictures the helper builds contained and the build prints a warning naming the files.
phonescompact | list | railcompactUnder 720px. compact: the current name's picture once, then the names as ruled rows of 48px or more (name and place; two columns from nine names); the sentences are not shown and stay each link's description. list (--phones-list): the long ruled list with a small picture and the sentence under each name (about 140px a name), for five to eight names whose sentences must be read there. rail (--phones-rail): the names as cards in one sideways row (picture, name, place, sentence; one and a third in view).
ratio3x2 | 1x1 | 4x5the form's ownThe frame's shape (--ratio-…, on the last four columns). Whatever is asked for, a frame that would show a picture larger than its own pixels at 1440 steps down to a square, then 3:2, with a build warning.
leadindex0The name that is current at rest.
reversebooleanfalse--reverse: the frame on the left (not in --backdrop).
gaptight | standard | chapterstandardThe section's seam above. A backdrop section is flush: its neighbours take the whole gap.
groundCanvas | NightCanvasNot in --backdrop, which is always Night.
<section class="nu-section nu-name-wall nu-name-wall--cols-2" aria-labelledby="h" data-dx-name-wall>
  <header class="nu-section-header nu-section-header--split-5" data-reveal>…</header>
  <div class="nu-name-wall__stage">
    <ul class="nu-name-wall__items" role="list" data-hover-group data-reveal>
      <li class="nu-name-wall__item"><a class="nu-name-wall__name" href="…" aria-describedby="h-note-1" data-hover data-hover-line>
        <span class="nu-heading nu-heading--h3">Boston</span><span class="nu-text nu-text--meta nu-name-wall__place">Massachusetts</span></a>
        <span class="nu-name-wall__thumb" aria-hidden="true"><img class="nu-image nu-image--1x1" src="…" alt=""></span>
        <p class="nu-text nu-text--small nu-name-wall__note" id="h-note-1">Established in 1898, our first campus…</p></li>
      …
    </ul>
    <div class="nu-name-wall__frame">
      <div class="nu-name-wall__pictures"><img class="nu-image nu-image--fill nu-name-wall__picture" src="…" alt="" aria-current="true">…</div>
      <div class="nu-name-wall__captions"><p class="nu-text nu-text--small nu-name-wall__caption" aria-hidden="true" aria-current="true"><span class="nu-name-wall__caption-name">Boston, Massachusetts</span> Established in 1898, our first campus…</p>…</div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
<!-- with script the lead name carries aria-current="true": that switches the pinned form on (from 960px).
     up to eight names: no --cols-2, names at nu-heading--h2. backdrop="contained": nu-name-wall--contained, data-mode="dark", names at nu-heading--h2. size="display": nu-name-wall--display, names at nu-heading--display-s.
     backdrop: class="nu-section nu-section--flush nu-section--bleed nu-name-wall nu-name-wall--backdrop" data-mode="dark";
     the pictures end with <span class="nu-scrim nu-scrim--full"></span><span class="nu-scrim nu-scrim--scene"></span> -->

Events

  • choose From 960px: pointer over a name or focus on it; on touch, the name crossing the middle of the window. The script moves aria-current between names, pictures and captions; the other names step back (data-hover-group) and the current name keeps its line drawn (data-hover-line).
  • click Each name's navigation.

Accessibility

  • Every name is a plain link at all times: one tap or Enter navigates; nothing needs a hover. Its target is 44px high or more at every width (the whole row in the list form).
  • Each link is aria-describedby its line, so the sentence is available without the picture.
  • No running text on the photograph: in --backdrop the line sits on a glass panel and only names and the heading are set on the picture, over a 65% scrim plus the scene scrim.
  • The pinned frame sits under everything the page pins (--pin-top).
  • Without script, and under 960px, the wall is a plain list: every name is visible and linked and every sentence shows under its name at reading size; the row is the link's target. Paper prints that list.
  • The caption in the frame repeats the sentence for sighted readers and is aria-hidden.
  • Reduced motion: pictures and captions swap without fading.

Usage

  • Use it for proper names of one to three words: it is the pattern for a set people scan by name (campuses, colleges).
  • For the Night statement use backdrop="contained": it holds every picture at its own pixels and about one window.
  • Pick the lead photograph on purpose: it is what the section looks like at rest.
  • On --backdrop, use only photographs that are sharp at full width (1920 × 1080 or more).
  • Sentences or long titles as names (use IndexRows).
  • Fewer than five names.
  • More than two statements on a page: --display and --backdrop each count as one.
  • Red on the current name on Night.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · Filmstripv0.1 · 2026-11-17

Filmstrip

A workhorse. A set of parallel items as tall 2:3 posters in one rail, each poster one link named by its title (an h3): its short title, an optional meta line and the cue on the photograph under a Scrim, its one line of text under the poster on the ground. A sibling of PosterRail with taller frames, on the shared rail: native scroll and snap, a progress line that follows the scroll, paddles that disable at the ends, 1:1 mouse drag. Three posters across from 960px with the fourth showing in the margin; one and a third on phones. The names stand on one line across the strip: where a title or a meta line may wrap, the helper gives that line a two-line slot on every poster (--title-2, --meta-2); nothing is clamped.

Level
Organism
Section pattern
Workhorse: conventional reading order, efficient with height; use as often as the page needs.
Class
.nu-filmstrip --four --title-2 --meta-2 __track __item __poster __frame __copy __meta __text
Composes
Section, SectionHeader, Image, Scrim, Heading, Text, ArrowLink, RailControls, Motion hooks
Used by
—
Found on
PosterRail (the worked example of a section pattern); DIRECTIONS.md: a filmstrip rail of tall posters; a rail you drag or page through; no text over busy pictures; 22a .cc posters; 22a co-op rail's ProgressLine

What is experiential learning at Northeastern?

Every part of your journey at Northeastern is built for immersive learning, innovation, and integrating emerging technologies, like AI, to enhance creativity and career readiness.

  • Fully integrated from day 1

    Your immersive learning experience starts the day you arrive—evolving with you and enriching your degree from beginning to end.

  • Unmatched opportunities

    You’re in control of your journey with experiential options that span types, locations, and durations.

  • Learning without boundaries

    Study, work, and immerse yourself in culture, exploring new contexts and applying your academic knowledge.

  • Most expansive co-op program

    Gain full-time immersive professional work experience that positions you for a post-graduate job and network for your future.

  • Excel at top companies

    A global network of 3,900+ employer partners—spanning industries and continents—that continually evolves to provide real-world problem solving with exceptional companies.

  • Dedicated support at every step

    Surrounded with professional guidance from day 1 to post-graduation, helping you choose the right opportunities for your academic journey.

Props

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
headingSectionHeaderrequiredAny variant, at h2; it sits on the content edge. Posters start on column lines 1, 5 and 9, so a split header's body lines up with the second poster.
items4–10 × { title, url?, image, alt, text?, cue?, meta?, focus? }requiredEach poster is one link (no url: a poster that is not a link). meta is one small line under the title on the poster; focus the picture's object-position. title (an h3 at h4 size, two lines at most) and cue sit on the poster's Night frame; text is the item's sentence under the poster (reading size, at most 36ch). The helper reads the pictures' pixel sizes: where a four-column poster (363 × 544 at 1440) would enlarge one, the strip is built four across (--four, 260 × 390) with a build warning.
nountextitemsWhat the paddles page through: “Previous stories”, “More stories”.
gaptight | standard | chapterstandardThe section's seam above, on the wrapper (nu-section--…). The page chooses it.
groundCanvas | NightCanvasdata-mode="dark" on the wrapper for Night.
<section class="nu-section nu-section--bleed nu-filmstrip" aria-labelledby="h" data-dx-rail>
  <header class="nu-section-header nu-section-header--split-5" data-reveal>…</header>
  <ul class="nu-filmstrip__track" role="list" data-reveal data-dx-rail-track>
    <li class="nu-filmstrip__item"><a class="nu-filmstrip__poster" href="…" data-hover draggable="false">
      <span class="nu-filmstrip__frame" data-mode="dark"><span data-hover-media><img class="nu-image nu-image--fill" src="…" alt="" draggable="false"></span><span class="nu-scrim nu-scrim--poster"></span>
        <span class="nu-filmstrip__copy"><span class="nu-heading nu-heading--h4">Fully integrated from day 1</span></span></span>
      <span class="nu-text nu-text--small nu-filmstrip__text">…</span></a></li>
    …
  </ul>
  <div class="nu-rail-controls" data-dx-rail-controls hidden>   <!-- RailControls (_dx.rail_controls); dx.js shows it -->
    <span class="nu-progress" aria-hidden="true" data-dx-rail-progress></span>
    <span class="nu-text nu-text--meta nu-rail-controls__count" data-dx-rail-count></span>   <!-- "1–3 of 10", written by dx.js -->
    <div class="nu-rail-controls__paddles">
      <button class="nu-icon-button nu-icon-button--outline" type="button" aria-label="Previous stories" data-dx-rail-prev></button>
      <button class="nu-icon-button nu-icon-button--outline" type="button" aria-label="More stories" data-dx-rail-next></button>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

Events

  • page A paddle scrolls to the next or previous screenful, landing on an item's edge; each paddle disables at its end.
  • drag Mouse drag scrolls the rail 1:1; on release it settles on the nearest item. The click that ends a drag is swallowed.
  • click Each item's navigation.

Accessibility

  • The rail is a list of links; Tab moves through them and scrolls each into view (the focus ring stands outside the card at the system offset: the track keeps a step of room above and below). Swipe, wheel and trackpad scroll it natively.
  • Paddles are real buttons named for what they page; a paddle that reaches its end while focused stays focusable and says aria-disabled, so the keyboard never drops out.
  • The progress line is decorative (aria-hidden) and follows the scroll itself; beside it the count says which items are in view of how many (1–3 of 10).
  • An item that takes the keyboard's focus while cut off by either edge is brought wholly into view. Controls show only when the rail can travel at least one item's width.
  • With a mouse the track shows the grab cursor wherever it is not a link; a drag never opens the card under the pointer.
  • Nothing moves by itself. Reduced motion: paddles jump instead of gliding, and the progress line is set when the scroll comes to rest instead of travelling with it. On paper the rail prints as a grid of every item.
  • Only a short title and cue sit on the photograph, on a poster Scrim over a Night frame on both grounds; check AA over the brightest photograph.

Usage

  • Use portrait pictures with the subject in the upper two thirds; the title sits on the lower third.
  • Keep titles to two lines.
  • Fewer than four posters.
  • A set people scan by name (campuses, colleges, offices): a rail shows three of them at a time; use IndexRows or NameWall.
  • Auto-advance, or loop the strip.
  • Running text on a poster: it goes under it.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · PortraitWallv0.1 · 2026-11-17

PortraitWall

A unit’s people as one picture: a gapless, full-bleed wall of square portraits, each a link to that person, with the name rising on a scrim on hover and focus. From 960px the heading slot holds columns 1–4 and the faces start on column 5 and run to the window’s edge. The strip variant is one row of 12 under a heading.

Level
Organism
Class
.nu-portrait-wall --strip --captioned __head __grid __face __name __title
Composes
Heading, Text, Image, ArrowLink
Used by
—

Events

  • click A face’s navigation to that person’s profile or roster anchor.

Accessibility

  • Each face is one link named by the person’s name and title (title visually hidden); the portrait is alt="".

  • The wall is a <ul>, so the count is announced.

Usage

  • Use every portrait the unit has, shot the same way; fill whole rows.
  • Link each face to the person, not the wall to a page.
  • A flattened collage image, or faces that link nowhere.
  • The picture wall as the only way to find a person: it shows no titles and, on touch, no names (use --captioned).
  • Rounded corners.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · MixedRailv0.1 · 2026-11-17

MixedRail

A workhorse. A rail of cards of two widths, wide features (six columns) and narrow ones (three), on one picture height, so the row has a rhythm instead of a count. It starts on the content edge and runs off the right of the window, on the shared rail: a progress line that follows the scroll, paddles that disable at the ends, 1:1 mouse drag. Each card is one link, named by its title (an h3), that reads title, meta, text, cue; the track is one grid of five rows and every card a subgrid of it, so those parts sit on shared lines across the row whichever parts a card has. Phones: the same rail, a wide card nearly filling the window and a narrow one at two thirds of it; --stack stacks the cards under 720px instead, every card the same way (a row with a small 4:5 picture beside its copy: a list never mixes full-width cards and rows), for three or four items that must all be read.

Level
Organism
Section pattern
Workhorse: conventional reading order, efficient with height; use as often as the page needs.

Composes
Section, SectionHeader, Image, Heading, Text, ArrowLink, RailControls, Motion hooks

Events

  • page A paddle scrolls to the next or previous screenful, landing on an item's edge; each paddle disables at its end.
  • drag Mouse drag scrolls the rail 1:1; on release it settles on the nearest item. The click that ends a drag is swallowed.
  • click Each item's navigation.

Accessibility

  • The rail is a list of links; Tab moves through them and scrolls each into view (the focus ring stands outside the card at the system offset: the track keeps a step of room above and below). Swipe, wheel and trackpad scroll it natively.
  • Paddles are real buttons named for what they page; a paddle that reaches its end while focused stays focusable and says aria-disabled, so the keyboard never drops out.
  • The progress line is decorative (aria-hidden) and follows the scroll itself; beside it the count says which items are in view of how many (1–3 of 10).
  • An item that takes the keyboard's focus while cut off by either edge is brought wholly into view. Controls show only when the rail can travel at least one item's width.
  • With a mouse the track shows the grab cursor wherever it is not a link; a drag never opens the card under the pointer.
  • Nothing moves by itself. Reduced motion: paddles jump instead of gliding, and the progress line is set when the scroll comes to rest instead of travelling with it. On paper the rail prints as a grid of every item.
  • Picture alt is empty unless it adds something; the title names the card.

Usage

  • Start with a wide card so the first screen has a lead.
  • Run a weak or low-resolution picture narrow.
  • All wide or all narrow cards (use PosterRail or Filmstrip).
  • Two wide cards in a row at 1440: the next card no longer shows.
  • A set people scan by name (campuses, colleges, offices): a rail shows three or four of them at a time; use IndexRows or NameWall.
  • Text on the pictures.

Northeastern Design System · Organism · UnevenGridv0.1 · 2026-11-17

UnevenGrid

A workhorse. Exactly three, four or five parallel items when a grid is right: one large lead and smaller cards of different widths and shapes in two unequal columns (seven and four, with a column of air), dealt so both columns end near the same line. The cards are in the markup in the order given (the reading order and the order on phones); each column packs from the top (the cards are floats on the page's column lines; the pair of a five is one block). Every card is one link, named by its title (an h3), that reads title, meta, text, cue under its picture. Not a bento and not equal columns. --stagger drops the right column one step; --reverse swaps the columns. Phones: every card the same way, a row with a small 4:5 picture beside its copy (the lead keeps its larger title): a list never mixes full-width cards and rows.

Level
Organism
Section pattern
Workhorse: conventional reading order, efficient with height; use as often as the page needs.

PracticeCycle

A process that repeats, drawn as a loop: the heading and the sentence naming who guides it in columns 1–4, three to five stages from column 5 under one strong rule (Light numeral, h3 at h4 size, one sentence), and a hairline that runs from the last stage back to the first carrying what happens next. Use it for co-op's prepare, work, reflect, return; use Steps for a sequence that ends.

—
Found on
Key messaging 2026-10-30, Experience pillar: 'Class, work and reflection form one loop' and the coordinator from the second-year prep course to the final assessment; group-b audit 1.5: the loop of class, work and reflection is never stated as the idea; Batch 1 Experiential Learning home

Canvas · light

Four stages · guide · return

How co-op works

Your co-op coordinator works with you at every stage, from the second-year prep course to the final assessment.

Inside co-op
  1. 1

    Prepare

    A co-op prep course in your second year, and goals you set with your coordinator.

  2. 2

    Work

    Four to six months, full time and usually paid, with no classes and no tuition.

  3. 3

    Reflect

    Write about what you did, graded on your own assessment and your employer's.

  4. 4

    Return

    Bring the questions the job raised back into the classroom.

Back to class, then around again

Prop / slotTypeDefaultNotes
headingHeading h2requiredNames the loop in the reader's words: How co-op works.
guideTextnoneOne or two sentences on who goes round with the reader (the co-op coordinator). Under the heading.
linkArrowLinknoneOne onward link under the guide.
stages3–5 × {title, text}requiredA verb or a short noun phrase each (Prepare, Work, Reflect, Return), and one sentence of fact. Numerals come from the order.

<section class="nu-practice-cycle" aria-labelledby="pc">
  <div class="nu-practice-cycle__head">
    <h2 class="nu-heading nu-heading--h2" id="pc">How co-op works</h2>
    <p class="nu-text">Your co-op coordinator works with you at every stage …</p>
  </div>
  <div class="nu-practice-cycle__body">
    <ol class="nu-practice-cycle__stages">
      <li class="nu-practice-cycle__stage"><span class="nu-numeral nu-numeral--md nu-practice-cycle__numeral" aria-hidden="true">1</span>
        <h3 class="nu-heading nu-heading--h4">Prepare</h3><p class="nu-text">…</p></li>
      …
    </ol>
    <p class="nu-practice-cycle__return"><span>Back to class, then around again</span></p>
  </div>
</section>

Events

  • None. Presentational only.

Accessibility

  • The stages are one <ol>; numerals are aria-hidden because the list counts.
  • The return line is drawn with borders; its label is real text and the arrow icon is hidden.

Usage

  • Keep every stage to one sentence so the four columns stay level.
  • Put the person who guides the loop beside it, not in a fifth stage.
  • A circle of icons or a rotating diagram: the line is enough.
  • Red on the loop: nothing here is current.
  • Use it for a one-way process such as applying.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · PartnerCasesv0.1 · 2026-11-17

PartnerCases

Two to four partnerships side by side, each as the research theme pages tell a case: the partner, where the work happens, the problem the partner brought, what was done together, one onward link. From 960px the cases share rows so every beat starts on the same line; three cases fall on columns 1, 5 and 9. Type only, under one strong rule each.

Canvas · light

Three cases

  • U.S. Army Research Laboratory

    Kostas Research Institute for Homeland Security · Burlington, Mass., and Arlington, Va.

    The problem
    The Army wanted a Northeast hub where it could co-locate staff alongside other experts to develop defense technologies and bring them to the battlefield faster.
    What we did
    The lab chose the Kostas Research Institute, where teams work on cybersecurity, tactical shelters, smart sensors and nanomaterials.
    Research partnerships

  • MaineHealth

    Roux Institute · Portland, Maine

    The problem
    Hospitals need better models for anticipating negative outcomes, so doctors and nurses can intervene earlier.
    What we did
    Researchers use data on ICU patients at Maine Medical Center to build algorithms that predict complications after heart surgery.
    Using AI to improve patient care

  • City of Boston

    Dukakis Center for Urban and Regional Policy · Boston

    The problem
    The city knew young people faced barriers to its summer jobs program, but had no data to show where.
    What we did
    An algorithm that helps Boston equitably place 9,000 young people in summer jobs.
    Community to Community

Northeastern Design System · Organism · AIJudgmentTracev0.1 · 2026-11-17

AIJudgmentTrace

Where AI does the work and where people decide, told as real projects step by step. Human judgment is the spine: a person's step (circle) sits on one vertical line, AI's step (square) branches off it and returns. A key and the list of three or four projects sit in columns 1–4; the open project's photograph, setup, NGN story and trace run from column 5. Built for the human-centered AI page; use it wherever a page has to show who does what in a process shared between people and a system.

Events

  • select a pick opens a case

Accessibility

  • The index is a vertical tablist (arrow keys, Home, End); each case a tabpanel labelled by its pick. Without script the picks are in-page links and every case is open in order.
  • The actor is always written (People decide / AI does the work); shape repeats it, colour never carries it alone.
  • Each pattern of markers has a text equivalent (role=img with the step counts).

Usage

  • Use one real story per case and link it with its own headline.
  • Keep the case setup to one sentence.
  • Keep it to the trace: no lens, tallies or summary lines. Zach 10-31: the first version was too busy.
  • Invent a step to make the pattern tidier.
  • Colour the AI lane red or put red on the spine: no actor is the marker.
  • Animate anything but opacity and transform; nothing moves under reduced motion.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · AIMajorIndexv0.1 · 2026-11-17

AIMajorIndex

A family of programs set as one sentence in display type: the shared root said once in Light at h2 size, every partner field after it as a link at h3 size, two columns from 720px, on hairlines. The count, one line of context and the onward link hang in columns 1–6; the sentence runs from column 7, the reading edge. Use it where the breadth of a family is the point (the 24 AI combined majors); for programs that need descriptions use LinkRows or Finder.

Northeastern Design System · Organism · ThemeExplorerv0.1 · 2026-11-17

ThemeExplorer

Research themes you can walk into: Tabs choose a theme, a picker of real projects (square thumbnail and the project's question) chooses one, and the project opens as a photograph, its question and two beats, Where and with whom and What it could change, over its source story. With no script it is a stacked feature: each theme's line and home campus in columns 1–4, all its projects from column 5.

  1. 1

    Your first week

    Meet your co-op coordinator

    Before you apply

GusGlobe

        <h2 class="nu-heading nu-heading--h1 nu-gus-globe__c …

Events

  • step The step whose text crosses 60% of the viewport becomes current (data-active): camera, route, lit campuses.
  • choose A pin, chip or link chose a campus: the globe turns to it, zooms for clustered campuses, labels fan out on leaders, the card opens.

Accessibility

  • The canvas is aria-hidden; every route is restated as a RouteLine and text, every campus as a card.
  • Chips are links to the campus cards, so they work with script off; the card is a labelled aside with a Close button, Escape closes it and focus returns to the control that chose the campus (a chip, a rail link; any element carrying data-gus-campus).
  • The globe turns by itself on some steps, so it carries a pause control (WCAG 2.2.2): a MediaControl toggle, always visible once the script runs, aria-pressed for its state, one unchanging name. It also holds still while a campus control is hovered or focused, while a card is open and while it is dragged.
  • Native scroll only. Reduced motion: the camera cuts, arcs appear whole, the globe starts held (the pause control shows play), step text is never dimmed.

Usage

  • One real route per path step.
  • Keep arcs in ink; the chosen campus is the one red mark, ringed.
  • Spokes from one campus to all the others.
  • Scroll-jacking or snapping.
  • Instructions on how to use it in the copy.

HeroStage

A workhorse hero for the Center leaning: the headline on the page's own ground on the centre axis, a short lead and one primary pill, and under them one wide stage carrying a film or photograph that rises from the fold, so the first screen holds headline, lead, action and the top of the picture. The stage runs the window's width (--inset: the content width); its picture drifts inside the frame. Phones stand the stage up at 4:5 so it holds the screen.

  <div class="nu-hero-stage__copy">
    <h1 class="nu-heading nu-heading--display nu-hero-stage__title" id="h">AI moves fast. You decide where to take it.</h1>
    <p class="nu-text nu-text--lead nu-hero-stage__lead">…</p>
    <div class="nu-hero-stage__actions"><a class="nu-button" href="…">Learn more </a></div>
  </div>
  <div class="nu-hero-stage__stage" data-reveal="unmask"><!-- a still: data-drift here and the <img class="nu-image nu-image--fill"> inside -->
    <div class="nu-film-player nu-film-player--fill" data-mode="dark" data-dx-player="loop" data-drift>… _dx.film(): video, poster, glass toggle (molecules/film-player) …</div>

Events

  • toggle { paused } from the film's pause control, on the stage's content edge (bottom left).

Accessibility

  • One h1; the section is labelled by it.
  • A film is the FilmPlayer (_dx.film, a loop; molecules/film-player): muted, it plays only while it is in view, starts on its poster, which cross-fades to the film once it shows a picture, and stays on the poster without script or under reduced motion. Its glass pause control (hairline ring, so it reads on bright and dark frames) shows whenever script runs, keeps one name and flips aria-pressed (pressed = paused).
  • The picture drifts a few percent inside its fixed frame as the frame crosses the window (data-drift): a CSS scroll-driven animation, still where unsupported or under reduced motion. No text moves.
  • A stage that starts below the fold arrives once by unmasking (data-reveal="unmask"); in a first screen it is simply there.
  • A decorative stage has alt=""; a picture that carries meaning gets real alt text.

Usage

  • Use the page's strongest wide picture or its film: this is the one hero-scale picture of the page.
  • Keep the copy short enough that the stage shows above the fold at 1440 by 900.
  • Set type on the stage. Text on a picture is HeroFrame's job.
  • Round the stage or put it in a card.
  • Follow it with another centred, full-width picture section.

The picture drifts inside the frame. With --chapters the frame stops one rail short of the window, so a ChapterRail placed straight after it reads as the frame's bottom edge. Events

  • toggle { paused } from the MediaControl.

Accessibility

  • One h1; the section is labelled by it.
  • A film is the FilmPlayer (_dx.film, a loop; molecules/film-player): muted, it plays only while it is in view, starts on its poster, which cross-fades to the film once it shows a picture, and stays on the poster without script or under reduced motion. Its glass pause control (hairline ring, so it reads on bright and dark frames) shows whenever script runs, keeps one name and flips aria-pressed (pressed = paused).
  • The picture drifts a few percent inside its fixed frame as the frame crosses the window (data-drift="strong" on __media): a CSS scroll-driven animation, still where unsupported or under reduced motion. No text moves.
  • Text stands on shade: over the scene scrim the copy lays one as tall as itself (the full Scrim under 960px, three fifths of it from 960px), and from 960px the aside in the right columns adds a shade tied to its own box, feathered a step beyond it; the picture above the copy stays lit. Measured over an all-white frame at 1440, 1024 and 390: the headline holds 3.3:1 or better at its worst pixel, the lead 10:1, an outline pill 11:1.
  • The pill is canvas on Night and the pause control is glass with a hairline ring; nothing here is red.
  • The pause control stands beside the pill; with no lead and no pill it stands alone on the frame's foot at the content's far edge.

Usage

  • Use films without burned-in text; the headline lives in HTML.
  • Let the page's header float over the frame (--over-media).
  • A headline longer than three lines at 1440.
  • A second pill.
  • Use it on a Read or Operate page: that is TitleCard.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · ChapterRailv0.1 · 2026-11-17

ChapterRail

The page's chapters as one hairline rail of anchor links, each chapter a stretch of the line. It sits straight under a full-bleed hero as that frame's bottom edge, then travels with the reader at the top of the window; the chapter being read is the lit stretch of the hairline (canvas on Night, red on Canvas), one marker that glides from chapter to chapter. Phones: the row scrolls sideways under a fade and keeps the current chapter in view. A workhorse; a thin bar that takes part in the rhythm as a flush section (a div: the nav is the landmark).

Events

  • click The page glides to the chapter (DX.glide; instant under reduced motion), the address follows, focus moves to the section, and the marker goes straight to the choice.

Accessibility

  • A nav with an ordered list of real links: it works without script.
  • The current chapter is aria-current="location"; the mark is a line and a text colour, never colour alone.
  • Each link is at least 56px tall; focus rings sit inside the row and appear at once.
  • From 960px two, three or four chapters start on the page's columns (1 and 7; 1, 5, 9; 1, 4, 7, 10; six on every second column from 1200px); five and seven share the row evenly.
  • Hover and press change the label's ink only; the marker moves for reading and for a choice, never for hover.
  • scroll-padding-top on the page keeps a target clear of the rail.

Usage

  • Put it first in <main>, straight after a HeroFrame --chapters.
  • Name chapters for what they hold, not for their order.
  • More than seven chapters: use a ContentsBar or a TableOfContents.
  • Numbers in front of the labels.
  • A second sticky bar on the same page.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · HeroOffsetv0.1 · 2026-11-17

HeroOffset

A statement hero for the Offset leaning: the headline at the largest display size low on the left across eight columns; a tall picture on the right four columns that leaves the grid at the top and at the right edge of the window; the lead and its primary pill under the headline on the headline's own edge (one reading edge), ending on the picture's foot. The picture drifts inside its frame. Below 960px: the picture first, edge to edge under the header (3:2 on phones, 16:9 on tablets), then headline, lead and pill on the content edge, all in the first screen.

Northeastern Design System · Organism · TitleCardv0.1 · 2026-11-17

TitleCard

A workhorse: the top of a Read or Operate page, where the type does the work and there is no picture. One title block in three placements: --center on the centre axis; --margin with the title large on the left eight columns and a margin column for the page's key links; --card, the Night title card, the left placement held low in a card whose height is capped by the window, so the header, the card and a contents bar fit one laptop screen. Each carries an optional trail, a short lead, one line of meta, pills and key links. Phones stack the block and set the key links under it as full-width rows.

Northeastern Design System · Organism · PullStatementv0.1 · 2026-11-17

PullStatement

A sentence pulled out of a paragraph, with the rest of the thought directly under it. Plain, the default, it is a workhorse: the sentence at h2 size on the content edge across nine columns, its lead and one onward link under it on the same edge, one block. With a picture (--inset) it is a statement: the sentence a size larger across ten columns with a small picture set into its first two lines the way a drop capital is, the lead and link close under it on columns 7–12, the reading edge, the lead filling its column. --end moves the block in by whole columns. Phones: one column; the inset picture sits small above the sentence.

Northeastern Design System · Organism · CloserOffsetv0.1 · 2026-11-17

CloserOffset

A workhorse closer for the Offset leaning: the closing line anchored low and left with its sentence and primary pill as one block, and one tall picture off to the right that leaves the grid at the window's edge; the block ends on the picture's foot and the picture gives the section its height. The picture drifts inside its frame. --reverse hangs the picture off the left edge. Below 960px: the picture first, edge to edge (3:2 on phones, 16:9 on tablets), then the line and the pill on the content edge, so the action is the last thing before the footer.

<div class="nu-section nu-section--tight nu-section--flush nu-section--bleed nu-contents-bar nu-contents-bar--center" data-dx-contents>
  <nav class="nu-contents-bar__nav" aria-label="On this page">
    <p class="nu-text nu-text--small nu-contents-bar__label" aria-hidden="true">On this page</p>
    <ol class="nu-contents-bar__list" role="list" data-indicator>
      <li><a class="nu-chip nu-contents-bar__link" href="#boston" aria-current="location">Boston campus</a></li>
      <li><a class="nu-chip nu-contents-bar__link" href="#commitment">Our commitment</a></li>
    </ol>
  </nav>
</div>

Events

  • click The page glides to the section; the pill goes straight to the choice.

Accessibility

  • A nav with an ordered list of real anchor links: it works without script.
  • The section being read is aria-current="location". One rule in every tracker (dx_heroes.js): it is the section whose heading most recently crossed the reading line, three tenths of the way down the window and never above the line a chosen section lands on; over the last stretch of the page the line runs down to the window's foot, so a short or late section still has its turn and the last one is current at the page's end. IntersectionObservers on the line, scrollend, hashchange and resize say when to look; nothing runs on scroll.
  • A chosen section (a contents link, any other link to it on the page, the address) keeps the mark until the reader moves the page, however short it is.
  • A choice glides to its section (DX.glide; instant under reduced motion), the address follows and focus moves there; the marker goes straight to the choice and stays on it while the page glides.
  • scroll-padding-top on the page is --pin-top plus --space-5: a target lands clear of everything that travels (the pinned unit header, a travelling SiblingNav and this bar, whose height is --contents-bar-h, set where the bar is on the page).
  • Sections after the bar read a --sticky-offset one bar taller, so their pinned parts (a StickyScenes frame, an IndexRows picture) park under it.
  • Pills are 44px tall; the row leaves room for a focus ring on every side.
  • Default, hover, focus, pressed and current are distinct: outline, tinted, ringed, settled, filled.

Usage

  • Put it straight after the TitleCard.
  • Use it for up to seven sections; beyond that, a TableOfContents beside the text.
  • Pills that wrap to a second row.
  • Use it for links to other pages: that is SiblingNav.

Northeastern Design System · Organism · OffsetPairv0.1 · 2026-11-17

OffsetPair

Two items, each a picture with its own short copy, in two forms. Stepped (the default, a statement): seven columns at 3:2 and four columns, the small one a step lower; from 960px the two pictures share a foot and the two blocks of copy start on one line, so nothing hangs under either. --even (a workhorse): the quiet two-up, six columns each, equal pictures, equal tops, titles on one line. The stepped pictures drift at two rates as the page scrolls; an item that is one link scales its picture on hover instead. On phones the small picture keeps its shape, narrower and pushed to the far edge, so the stagger survives the stack; the even pair stacks whole.

Organism
Section pattern

      <div class="nu-picture-band__actions"><a class="nu-button" href="…">Learn more </a></div>

</section>

Events

  • click The pill's navigation.
  • film The FilmPlayer's own.

Accessibility

  • The picture is decoration unless it adds something: empty alt.
  • Checked on rendered pixels with the text removed (worst pixel behind each line): 6:1 or better on the demo photographs at 320, 390, 768 and 1440; over a pure white picture the line keeps 3:1 or better (large type) and the lead 4.5:1 or better at every width up to 1920px (below 960px the veil is the whole Scrim: 5.6:1).
  • A film loop is paused by its toggle and stays on its poster under reduced motion.

Usage

  • Use it once or twice a page, where the subject changes.
  • Pick a picture with a calm area where the line sits.
  • Paragraphs on a picture.
  • A second pill, or red text (never on Night).
Northeastern Design System · Organism · SiblingNavv0.1 · 2026-11-17

SiblingNav

A workhorse: the pages of one section as one quiet row of links under the hero ("About: Leadership, Global university system, …"), the page being read marked. It is SectionNav's horizontal row as a section pattern: a flush, bleed bar on the page's edge. Built like the bars that carry a page's contents (ChapterRail's height, hairline and 2px marker) and read as the way to other pages: the section's name leads the row, the page being read is Medium, and its marker sits on the bar's foot, the header's current-page mark. The marker is one rule that rests under the current page and glides to the link in hand, then back. --travel parks the bar at the top of the window; what follows pins under it. A row wider than the bar scrolls sideways under a fade on the side that has more.

Level
Organism
Section pattern
Workhorse: conventional reading order, efficient with height; use as often as the page needs.

Composes

Events

  • hover, focus The marker glides to the link under the mouse or the keyboard and back to the current page when it leaves (instant under reduced motion; nothing follows a finger).
  • click The link's navigation.

Accessibility

  • A nav named for the section, holding a list of real links: it works without script (the current page keeps its own rule).
  • The current page is aria-current="page": Medium weight and the marker, never colour alone; red on Canvas, canvas on Night.
  • Links are 64px tall (56px under 960px); the focus ring sits inside the row, clear of the label, and appears at once.
  • Default, hover, focus, pressed and current are distinct: quiet ink, full ink with the marker, ringed with the marker, settled ink, Medium with the marker at rest.
  • A row wider than its bar scrolls sideways (touch, trackpad, keyboard focus); the side that has more fades, and the current page starts in view.

Usage

  • Put it straight after the hero (hero_stage(flush="bottom"), hero_frame(chapters=True)), the same row on every page of the section.
  • Let it travel on long pages whose readers move between the section's pages; leave it in place on short ones.
  • Carry the Breadcrumb in the hero (trail=), not in this row.
  • Anchors to sections of this page: that is ChapterRail or ContentsBar.
  • A travelling SiblingNav and a contents bar on one page unless the page is long enough to need both (they stack: 128px).
  • Chips or pill Buttons for sibling pages (they read as filters or calls to action).
  • More than seven pages: use SectionNav beside the content.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · CallListv0.1 · 2026-11-17

CallList

A workhorse: the numbers a page exists to give, set as type. Each row is one number: who it reaches on the left four columns, the number from column 5 at display size (eight columns for the number and its controls; a stacked header above it) as a tap-to-call link, a Copy control after it (from 960px every Copy of the list stands in one column, after the longest number), and any further lines (fax, TTY, hours, a link) under it. The first row is the one to call first: a size larger, with the page's single red mark, a rule under the number (canvas on Night). Phones stack who, number and Copy.

Events

  • copy { number }: the number is on the clipboard; the control cross-fades to a check and Copied (data-dx-copy-done), returns by itself after a moment, and a status line says so. A press while it reads Copied copies again and restarts the moment. If the clipboard refuses, the number is selected instead.
  • click The number dials (tel:).

Accessibility

  • Every number stands on a rule, so it reads as a link at rest: a hairline (redrawn in ink on hover and focus), and the page's one red rule under the number to call first, which answers too (it is redrawn from the left in ink, a hairline heavier; on Night the canvas rule thickens). The focus ring stands clear of the rule.
  • Each number is a real tel: link at least 64px tall, named by its digits; its hairline draws on hover and focus.
  • The Call pill repeats the number's link for a thumb: it is aria-hidden and out of the tab order, so keyboard and screen-reader users meet each number once.
  • Copy is a button named ‘Copy’ plus the number (the name does not change); it is hidden until script can reach the clipboard, and the result is announced through a polite status region.
  • Copy's states are distinct: outline at rest, filled on hover, ringed on focus, settled when pressed, a check and Copied when done.
  • The red rule is never the only signal: the first number is first and larger. On Night the rule is canvas.
  • Nothing here arrives on scroll: the reader came for these numbers.

Usage

  • Put the number to call in an emergency first.
  • Keep name to what the number reaches, in the words people search for.
  • A second marked number on the page.
  • Icons in front of the numbers, or cards around them.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · MarginFiguresv0.1 · 2026-11-17

MarginFigures

A tall picture with the section's heading and figures as one block beside it. The picture holds six columns (its ratio is the caller's: 4:5 usually); the block (heading, an optional lead and further paragraphs, two to four figures as a short ruled list, their source) holds five, a column apart, and stands with its cap height on the picture's top edge (or centred, or on its foot): never split between the two ends of the column. From 960px the picture grows to the block's height when the block is the taller, so the two end together. The source order is always heading, lead, figures, picture. Phones: picture, heading, then the figures as a ruled list; with --reverse the block first and the picture last.

Workhorse: conventional reading order, efficient with height; use as often as the page needs.

Northeastern Design System · Organism · FigureSlatev0.1 · 2026-11-17

FigureSlate

A Night title card of figures: large numerals, each over its own sentence. No rules, no list, nothing ranged against an axis: the numerals are the picture and the title names it (StatBand is the Canvas figures pattern; the two never look alike). Numerals at display-s, one clear step above the h2 title. The card is laid out by the number of figures, so no cell is empty. Two, four or six: the title, its lead and the one pill stand in the left margin (four columns) and the figures stand two across from the fifth column line. Three: the title on columns 1 to 4 with its lead beside it, the three figures in one row on columns 1, 5 and 9, the pill under them. Five: the title block is the first cell of a three-by-two card. 720 to 960: the title on top, figures two across (three for three); phones: one column.

PortraitSet

Three to five people at real scale, never a row of equal small cards. Three stand as a staircase on five, four and three columns, portraits sharing a floor and names a baseline. Northeastern Design System · Organism · StoryRailv0.1 · 2026-11-17

StoryRail

Northeastern Global News stories in one native scrolling row that starts on the content edge and runs off the right of the window. The first story leads on six columns at 3:2 with its headline at h3 size; the others stand on four columns (a headline needs that much), their pictures cropped to the lead's height, so the rail is one band of pictures over one line of headlines. It is the shared rail: under it RailControls, a progress line that follows the scroll and two paddles that disable at the ends; the row also drags with the mouse. Phones: the lead fills most of the width and the next story shows at the edge.

Events

  • scroll The progress line follows the scroll itself (a CSS scroll-driven animation; set at rest where that is unsupported); a paddle is disabled at its end.
  • page A paddle brings the first story that is not fully in view to the content edge, or goes back one screenful (instantly under reduced motion). The shared rail: build/js/dx.js, [data-dx-rail].

Accessibility

  • The row scrolls natively: swipe, wheel, Shift + wheel, and Tab moves through the stories and brings each into view. Nothing moves by itself.
  • The controls are shown by script and only when the row overflows; without script the row still scrolls.
  • A paddle that reaches its end while it holds focus stays focusable (aria-disabled) until focus leaves it, so the keyboard never drops out of the rail; the progress line is decoration.

Usage

  • Lead with the newest or strongest story.
  • Set each picture's focus if its subject is off centre: the others are cropped tall.
  • Auto-advance.
  • Fewer than four stories (use StoryLead).
Northeastern Design System · Organism · LogoRowv0.1 · 2026-11-17

LogoRow

One quiet row of partners' marks on the centre axis: no cells, no rules, every mark set to the same optical weight and one colour, so the row reads as one grey line on Canvas and on Night. From 960px up to eight marks share one line and more take two (--rows), so no mark is squeezed; below that they wrap, centred, and never leave one mark alone on a phone's last line. --marquee is the same row as a slow rail (one linear translate, --dur-loop per mark) with a visible pause toggle; it rests under the pointer and focus and is the still row under reduced motion and without script. A mark that is a link makes the others step back while it is under the pointer or holds focus.

<section class="nu-section nu-logos" aria-labelledby="h">
  <header class="nu-section-header nu-section-header--center" data-reveal>…</header>

      <li class="nu-logos__item" style="--mark-ratio:2.41"><div class="nu-logo-tile"><img class="nu-logo-tile__mark" src="…" alt="BCG"></div></li>

Events

  • toggle aria-pressed on the pause toggle (pressed = paused). The rail also rests while the pointer or focus is on it.

Accessibility

  • A list of images named by partner; the copies the script adds to close the loop are aria-hidden and out of the tab order.
  • Reduced motion and no script: the marks wrap into the still, centred row and the toggle is not shown.
  • Marks are one colour through --mark-filter, so dark logos stay legible on Night.

Usage

  • Trim every file to its artwork and state its ratio.
  • Use the marquee only for a long list that is proof by volume.
  • Full-colour logos at rest.
  • A second row (use LogoWall for a wall).
Northeastern Design System · Organism · CampusGlobev0.1 · 2026-11-17

CampusGlobe

A workhorse. A set of places as a ruled list of names (each a link) beside a small globe. Pointing at or focusing a name turns the globe to it in one ease of --dur-scene and marks it red with its name; pointing at or tapping a mark lights its name (aria-current). The globe never turns by itself unless tour=True (it then visits each place in turn, with a MediaControl pause, held under reduced motion). From 960px the heading and names on columns 1-5, the globe on 7-12 (--reverse swaps); phones: heading, the globe with its lower third cut, then the names. Without script the globe is a still SVG with every place marked. When to use a map, and when the NameWall list: the list where people scan by name and a picture helps them choose; a map where breadth or geography is the point, or where the photographs are weak. CampusBand puts the geography into a NameWall's heading.

Level
Organism
Section pattern
Workhorse: conventional reading order, efficient with height; use as often as the page needs.

Northeastern Design System · Organism · CampusAtlasv0.1 · 2026-11-17

CampusAtlas

A workhorse. A flat map of North America (Albers equal-area) cropped to the set, a place across the Atlantic in a framed inset in the first clear corner; land a step off the ground, lakes cut out, borders as hairlines, edges fading into the ground. Each place an ink mark with its label, placed so that none collides (one that cannot stand clear is left off, never the chosen one). With script the names are a vertical tablist under the map (three columns, read down) and the chosen place shows a panel beside: square photograph, place, name, sentence, link; the chosen mark is the single red one, ringed. Phones: map, panel (picture beside copy), names in two columns. Without script: the map with every mark, then every place's name, sentence and link. When to use a map, and when the NameWall list: the list where people scan by name and a picture helps them choose; a map where breadth or geography is the point, or where the photographs are weak. CampusBand puts the geography into a NameWall's heading.

Northeastern Design System · Organism · GlobeViewv0.1 · 2026-11-17

GlobeView

The one globe of the globes family: an orthographic sphere drawn per pixel by one WebGL shader from an inlined land field (Natural Earth, baked at build time), finished like a product render: exact tones, crisp antialiased coast and hairline limb, no halo, never a texture. One style: flat (two exact tones; the default), solid (lit land, quiet coast), studio (one wide soft light, land a hair lighter than the sea), ink (the continents as a clean silhouette), mono (land and sea one tone apart, the red marks a touch larger). Marks crisp and round with one ring; names in the DOM, clustered and never over a mark. Colours are the ground's tokens. Without script or WebGL, a still SVG of the same view.

Organism

Northeastern Design System · Organism · GlobeChaptersv0.1 · 2026-11-17

GlobeChapters

Chapters of a set on columns 1-5 scroll past a globe pinned on 7-12. A chapter is current from the moment its top crosses the middle of the window; the globe is scrubbed by the scroll between chapters (rotation and zoom eased, a slight pull-back on long moves), closes in inside its resting disc (at most 1.6×) to frame the chapter's campuses, and their marks rise in from ink to red. It rises a little as the section enters and drifts a fraction of a degree at rest. Phones: the globe pinned at the top. No script and reduced motion: nothing pinned.

Events

  • None. Presentational only.

Accessibility

  • The names are the content: each a real link, in order, all in the tab order; the globe, its marks and labels are aria-hidden.
  • Focus does what pointing does; one current-state mark per list; focus rings on :focus-visible only.
  • Reduced motion: no drift, no flights, no pinning, no scrub; the complete still state.

Usage

  • Use one globe a page, where the reach of the network is the point; look from the north.
  • Lines between places (arcs, routes, connections); line-drawn land (hatching, outline-only coasts); any surface texture (grain, noise, paper, halftone, misregistration: Zach 11-13, "sleek and clean, not more random textures"); a globe cut by its container (GlobeHorizon's planet wider than the window is the one exception); a southern-hemisphere view; two globe patterns on one page.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · MilestoneTrackv0.1 · 2026-11-17

MilestoneTrack

A giant word behind (the h2); framed cards at staggered heights (square), each with a title and one tabular stat line; under them a ruler that travels with them: a yard line through every card, minor ticks between, and the card's number set large (01, 02 …). From 960px, motion allowed and when the cards overflow, the stage pins and one transform carries the row right to left as the page scrolls; a card that takes focus brings its place into view. A linked card shows a pointer label; its picture scales inside its frame. Resting form (phones, reduced motion, no script): a row that scrolls sideways with snap points, the ruler along its foot.

Level
Organism
Section pattern
Statement: expressive, spends a screen on one idea; two per page at most.

Events

  • scroll data-dx-flex-track: pins and carries the row (eased follow, about 120ms).
  • focus A focused card brings its place on the page into view; nothing traps focus.
  • pointer data-dx-flex-cursor shows the label; nothing tilts.

Accessibility

  • An ordered list of links; the resting row is a labelled, focusable region.
  • The numbers are aria-hidden (the list numbers itself) and hold 3:1 as large text.

Usage

  • Six to fourteen cards.
  • Invent a figure for a stat line.
  • Two tracks on one page.
Northeastern Design System · Organism · ShowcaseStagev0.1 · 2026-11-17

ShowcaseStage

A pinned stage, one item a screen of scroll: the giant word behind (the h2); the subject in the middle changing per item (one framed picture, or two or three prints stepped apart, square); on the left a vertical dot pager beside the item's name, three or four lines and its link; along the foot a rail of names or marks moving in step with the current entry in full ink; a view-all pill bottom right. Resting form (no script, reduced motion): the items stacked, picture beside copy. Phones: the same stage with the pager across the foot and no rail.

F.showcase_stage(e(word), [(name, text, [(image, alt, focus)], (label, url)), …], "stage", view_all=(label, url))

Events

  • scroll data-dx-flex-stage: the current item follows the scroll; the rail is one transform.
  • dot A dot (a button named by its item) glides the page to that item.
  • focus A link inside an item that takes focus brings its item on stage.

Accessibility

  • Every item stays in the reading order and its link in the tab order; nothing is inert or trapped.
  • Dots carry aria-current for the item on stage; the rail is decorative (aria-hidden).

Usage

  • Sets of parallel things with a strong picture each: research areas, programmes, places, partner work.
  • People profiles: never (Zach, 11-13).
  • More than eight items (use IndexRows).
Northeastern Design System · Organism · PhotoMarqueev0.1 · 2026-11-17

PhotoMarquee

A big centred heading over an endless rail of square paper prints at staggered heights, each with a small caption on its foot. It drifts left slowly (one linear transform, --dur-loop per print) and rests under the pointer, under focus, out of view and when its pause toggle is pressed. Resting form (no script, reduced motion): the same prints in a row that scrolls sideways.
